ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Code to Enrol user on a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Not got complete answer yet, but it looks as though the approved method is to create a class 'your_class' extending from class enrol_plugin (see Enrolment Plugins ) and then call your_class::enrol_user(); These are the comments from enrol_plugin::enrol_user with some notes of my own. /** * Enrol user into course via enrol instance. * * @param stdClass $instance (instance class contains id => enrolid, courseid => course_id) * @param int $userid * @param int $roleid optional role id * @param int $timestart 0 means unknown * @param int $timeend 0 means forever * @param int $status default to ENROL_USER_ACTIVE for new enrolments, no change by default in updates * @param bool $recovergrades restore grade history * @return void */

ResponsesInList.Title: IMS Enterprise - Group Unenrollment?
ResponsesInList.Text: Currently the IMS Enterprise Plugin does an excellent job of enrolling and unrolling students from a course. It also has the nice feature of being able to place students into groups when they are enrolled (based on the information provided in the XML file). What the plugin does not have a way of handling, however, is moving students from one group to another. Let me provide an example of where this would be needed: Note: Our courses are unique to Course + Teacher. Course sections are created as groups within the course. Student John Smith enrolls in Math 101 with Professor X. He is enrolled in section 03. This information is included in the XML file, and the plugin will correctly enroll him in the course, within section (group) 03. The following week, John Smith drops section 03 but enrolls in section 05 which is also taught by Professor X. Same course, same professor, different section. The plugin will place him in section (group) 05, but also leaves him in section (group) 03. I tried to program around this by unenrolling the student and then re-enrolling the student. However, this becomes a problem if the course has groups that were not created by the plugin. If anyone has any thoughts on how to program around this limitation I am definitely open to suggestions. Thanks in advance!

ResponsesInList.Title: SQL injection in external database enrol plugin?
ResponsesInList.Text: We use a modified version of the external database plugin for our enrolments.  Looking through the code, I found several things that raised concerns for me: User-entered fields like $localcoursefield are concatenated into queries with no validation (lib.php, 341, e.g.). The db_get_ sql function does not validate the $table, $fields, or $sort arguments; the first two of these can contain user input. The dbsetupsql config option allows a user to execute any SQL statement against the external database. Granted, the only users who have access to these input fields are site admins.  However, I'm thinking: first, what if someone hacks an admin's password; second, allowing SQL injection is generally a bad thing anyway. Am I seeing this right?  I'd like to get confirmation before starting a Tracker issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SQL injection in external database enrol plugin?
ResponsesInList.Text: Upon looking at it again, I realized that #1 isn't true: the local course field is selected from a drop-down, so users cannot enter arbitrary values. However, #2 is still valid.  For example, line 366 calls db_get_sql, passing array($coursefield) as the $fields argument.  But $coursefield is simply the remotecoursefield config entry with whitespace trimmed.  This config option is a text box that allows arbitrary input. Also, #3 remains unchanged.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SQL injection in external database enrol plugin?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, IMHO , you are seeing it right. #2 could probably be tightened, but I'd say #3 is not going to be so easily removed. Unfortunately some people need to execute some external-db-specific SQL code before Moodle can get data in a proper encoding. And catering for all the posible alternatives from the Moodle side is not that easy. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SQL injection in external database enrol plugin?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the confirmation, Iñaki.  Next question: if #3 (the obvious hole) is not easily fixable, is it still worth opening a Tracker issue for #2 (less obvious)? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Including self-enrol (only cohort members) in multiple courses
ResponsesInList.Text: You can create a cohort in a category but as far as I know, you can't assign a cohort to a category...but you can assign teacher roles to categories. At the site level, it is Administration (Settings in 2.3)>Users>Permissions>assign system roles.  This gives everyone assigned to the role those permissions in every course/category.  At the category level, it is Administration>Assign Roles.  This gives everyone assigned to the role in the category those permissions in every course/sub category in that category. ResponsesInList.Title: A bug in PayPal enrollment? Users able to access a course without paying.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello gang! I'm scrolling through the discussions and haven't seen this particular issue mentioned by anyone else. I've been having this problem for a few years actually and still haven't been able to pin down exactly what it is - but fortunately have some honest users who have brought it to my attention. I *think* the issue is this - A user will register on my website, then they'll go to look at a course. They will click on the "PayPal" button and then back out without paying. They then have full access to the course. I have had some others who say they registered and were never presented with the PayPal link to access any of the courses and they have full access, but I don't have any details on how that happens. My website - www.ASLwithRobNielson/moodle Thanks for your help! Rob

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A bug in PayPal enrollment? Users able to access a course without paying.
ResponsesInList.Text: A user that reported the issue to me just sent me an email with how she was able to access the lessons without paying. Here is what she did: Module 1 1. Went to " http:// www.ASLwithRobNielson.com ", 2. Clicked the "Everyone else that wants to learn ASL!" link, 3. Logged in, 4. "American Sign Language Courses" - "ASL - MODULE ONE", 5. Clicked "Send payment via PayPal" - No response, 6. Clicked PayPal icon - No response, 7. Clicked "Enrol me" link 8. Took me to Module 1 lessons page. 9. Lets me watch all lessons. At that point, I thought maybe you pay for each video right before you watch it. After I finished the lessons and it still didn't prompt payment, I figured I should contact you. I decided to see if it would work with the second one so I could more accurately describe what happened.Module 2 1. Went to " http:// www.ASLwithRobNielson.com ", 2. Clicked the "Everyone else that wants to learn ASL!" link, 3. Logged in, 4. "American Sign Language Courses" - "ASL - MODULE TWO", 5. Clicked "Send payment via PayPal" 6. Waited longer than before 7. PayPal loaded to pay screen 8. Figured bug did not affect Module 2 9. Pressed back button (I don't want Module 2 yet) 10. Took me to Module 2 lessons page 11. Lets me watch lessons So it looks like my initial suspicion is correct - if a user clicks on the PayPal button, then backs out without paying, they have full access to the lessons. This is definitely a bug. Suggestions on where I can report this particular bug to be fixed?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upload users connection timeout
ResponsesInList.Text: You will need to change the timeout settings in your php settings.  This is done on the server and not through the web interface.  I would start by upping the max_execution_time - mine is currently set to 360.  This setting on a linux is found in the /etc/php5/apache2/php.ini file. You might look at cohorts for your enrollment.  Seems like a lot of work to enroll in so many courses.  With cohorts, you can enroll a whole bunch of students into several courses at once.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 2.5 LDAP enrolment error
ResponsesInList.Text: I found the following post in another forum: Moodle 2.1 LDAP enrolment error Please save me from tearing my hair out! What happens in that case is that when a user logs in they are unenrolled from all their courses if they were enrolled in them via LDAP. (perhaps it sees the groups but believes they are not in it?) I've rolled back the version of Moodle and undone all the changes made, but its still broken, nothing has changed with AD etc and I've triple checked all the settings in Moodle. Thoughts or ideas would be appreciated! We face the same problem after we updated from 2.3 to 2.5. Does anbody have an idea how to resolve this error?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teacher as a student

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teacher as a student
ResponsesInList.Text: I have two suggestions, one for incidental need to create a course, one for bulk handling: If you want to create courses when users ask for it, please look at the Course Request page in Site Admin. If you enable Course Request, every user may ask for a course and has to fill in some details in the course request form. After submitting this form, the system sends it to the manager you had in mind. The latter reviews the form and if he/shee accepts it the course is created automatically, including adding the person who requested it as teacher. If you want to create courses in bulk, create a sprteadsheet with course short name, course long name, course category, teacher user name, split it into two separate spreassheets one for " Upload courses" (from Moodle 2.6) to create the courses, and one for "Upload users" to give existing users the role of teacher in their own course.

ResponsesInList.Text: If anyone is still having this problem, I found another discussion that lead me to a solution for this problem https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=177130 Basically it seems that the error is being caused by the calls to message_send() in the ipn script. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error when trying to view enrolled users
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Marko, if you're still interested I resolved the issue just this week. In our case it was due to an entry in mdl_enrol that didn't correspond to a cohort in mdl_cohort. Mdl_enrol contains a column called customint1 which contains the cohort id for each cohort that is synced to enrol onto a course. select id, courseid, customint1 from mdl_enrol where coursed = <the problem course id> I used the list of customint values returned from the above query from our problem course to check for records in mdl_cohort and found that one customint value in mdl_enrol didn't exist in mdl_cohort. ResponsesInList.Title: Removing users from a cohort
ResponsesInList.Text: I enrolled students in many courses using a cohort. Now I want to unenroll these students deleting them from the cohort. How can I do it? They don't appear in the ‘Current users’ field bechause there are more then 100 students.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Removing users from a cohort
ResponsesInList.Text: The straightforward method would be: search the users in the left container one-by-one and move them to the right container. However, that is a time consuming job. My suggestion would be: Create a new and temporary cohort. Go to Site admin / Users / Accounts / Bulk user actions. Try to formulate criteria to select the users who should STAY in your original cohort. Go to the bottom of the page and add the selected users to the new temporary cohort. Add an enrolment method for this cohort to all the courses where your original cohort was used AFTER completion of the previous task,you may delete entirely the original cohort next, you rename the temporary cohort and give it the name of the original cohort Why these steps? I assume that selecting the staying users takes less time, than removing the "wrong" ones manually. Further, unenrolling and handling user data are complex issues. I want to avoid mistakes by misinterpreting the documentation. So, I add the new cohort first, and remove the old cohort later. By the way, this suggestion seems to fail if your cohort has been enrolled in many courses. Then, adding the cohort enrol method many times becomes the bottleneck. The good news is that Moodle 2.6 has an interesting " upload courses" feature, comparable to the well-known update users feature. The "upload course" feature also works with existing courses. It can be used for uploading enrollment methods as well. Unfortunately, uploading the cohort enrolment method is either not well documented or buggy or both. Please, vote for mdl bug tracker https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-43127 to have this solved asap en make this power tool available for us all.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Auto enrolment using Active Directory groups
ResponsesInList.Text: Hiya, As Patrick says, the script should be extracted into moodle/local/ldap, you shouldn't need to overwrite anything. If you have backups I would suggest rolling back and placing the script in the suggested place. My values for the script are as follows: Verbose mode: unchecked Group attribute: cn Group class: group Real user class: sAMAccountName Process nested groups: checked Auto create missing cohorts: checked Everything under the "Synch Moodle's cohorts with LDAP attribute" title is then left as is. I'm assuming at this point you are also using LDAP Authentication. If this is the case you will need to check under Site Administration > Plugins > Authentication > LDAP Authentication and make sure the 'Contexts' has an ou of the location in AD where your groups you want to create exist e.g ou=Groups,dc=example,dc=local. A couple of other things to note. I'm pretty sure the ID number specified under the LDAP Authentication settings (as above) has to match the 'Real user class:' specified above, however the value input in LDAP Authentication will reformat itself on submission where as the setting for 'Real user class:' is case sensitive and needs to be as specified. Be aware this script will make cohorts for all groups with users in under the context you entered, which may extend the running time of the script. If you don't need all the groups you may want to look at making an dedicated ou for moodle groups. I'm using LDAP enrolment as well at the moment, if this is something you want to look into or need help with then just ask.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Providing Cohort Sync Enrolment Method Permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, I figured it out so I thought I'd pass along the answer in case anyone else ever needs it. First of all, I was actually using Moodle 2.0.2+ (build 20110420) Secondly, here are the directions for creating a user role that can create course and create/edit cohort groups at the category level. REF: http://docs.moodle.org/22/en/Capabilities/enrol/cohort:config - permissions list needed for course cohort management. 1. Log into Moodle as a site admin 2. Go to Site administration - Users - Permissions - Define Role 3. Click the "x2" icon to the right of the "course creator" role in order to make a copy of it 4. Name the role = "Cohort Manager" 4. Set role archetype = ARCHETYPE:Course Creator 5. Set Context types where this role may be assigned = "System" & "Category" NOTE: The default permissions for a "course creator" role will be broken down below the "Context types where this role may be assigned" field. You can override the default settings to created a tailored role that has the ability to manage category-based cohort groups. 6. Set the change default permissions as follows: - Role assignments synchronised to course enrolment enrol/category:synchronised = allow - Add and remove cohort members moodle/cohort:assign = allow - Create, delete and move cohorts moodle/cohort:manage = allow - Configure cohort instances enrol/cohort:config = allow

Go to Site administration - Users - Permissions - Define Role 3. Click the icon to the right of the "course creator" role in order to modify it. In my school, every course creator must enrol his students in his own course. 4. Set Context types where this role may be assigned = "System" & "Category". Likely, it is already ok. 5 . Set the change default permissions as follows: - Role assignments synchronised to course enrolment enrol/category:synchronised = allow - Configure cohort instances enrol/cohort:config = allow - Configure enrol instances in courses moodle/course:enrolconfig = allow - View site-wide cohorts moodle/cohort:view = allow Actually I'm using moodle 2.5, and I need only these four settings to permit the teacher the enrolment by cohort.

ResponsesInList.Title: User Enrolment Expiry
ResponsesInList.Text:
How can I find the current user's expiry date on the current course? I've started writing a block which is intended to do this but I'm struggling with the SQL . $sql = "SELECT enrol.enrolstartdate, enrol.enrolenddate FROM {enrol}
INNER JOIN {user_enrolment} ON user_enrolment.enrolid= enrol.id WHERE user_enrolment.userid=? AND enrol.courseid=?"; $result = $DB->get_record_sql($sql,  array($USER->id, $COURSE->id) ); This doesn't work. Any ideas anyone please? Cheers Dave

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User Enrolment Expiry
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Dave, If you’ve set the expiry date of the enrolment  for students, you’ll get the expiry date from mdl_user_enrolments table with a column named "timeend" with respect to each other. And if you’ve  set the enrolment period for course, you’ll get the expiry date from mdl_enrol table with a column named "enrolperiod". The query will look like: $sql = "select mdl_enrol.enrolperiod as course_expiry_date, mdl_user_enrolments.timeend as user_course_expiry_date from mdl_enrol join mdl_user_enrolments on mdl_user_enrolments.enrolid = mdl_enrol.id where mdl_courseid=? and mdl_user_enrolments.userid=?"; I hope this’ll help you to resolve your issue. Cheers! Purnendu DualCube

ResponsesInList.Title: Self enrolment problem - solved - Moodle 2.5
ResponsesInList.Text: This wasted about 2 hours of my time  ... so it may help someone else. We recently upgraded  our Moodle from 1.9 to 2.2 and then did a course by course import into  2.5 (our database had issues as it dated from v1.08 in 2003). Our students arrived this week and the self enrolment plugin failed 'You can not enrol yourself in this course' - even though site and course self enrolment settings seemed fine. The solution seems very strange but, with lots of trial and error as I couldn't find the solution on this forum, goes like this: Go into the course (logged in as teacher/admin): Course admin>users>enrolment methods>self enrolment> set 'Unenrol inactive after' to 'never' rather than our default '365 days'. Save. Self enrolment now works and students see the 'enrol' button when they click on the course to enter. Even more strangely, self enrolment continued to work even if I put the setting back to 365 days later!!!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Self enrolment problem - solved - Moodle 2.5
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks so much for posting this issue and solution. I had exactly the same issue with courses imported from a 2.3 to a2.5 site. All the 'Unenrol inactive after' dates were set to 'Never' and setting them to 1800 days then gets self-enrollment working again. So it looks like just changing the setting will then "correct" the issue. This is obviously a bug in the way that setting is restored and so it appears that the Unenroll inactive dates are passed for everyone. I restored this course with existing users in it. That may be an interesting variable.

ResponsesInList.Title: Unable to load new courses using LMB 2.5.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I've been fighting with this for a while now.  I installed Moodle 2.5.1 along with LMB 2.5.1 (and older version) on my devel. server .  I cannot load the courses into Moodle using this plug in.  Nothing registers in the log file other than this line: The import log will appear below.  The same xml file will work just fine in Mooddle 1.9.16/LMB 0.8.5.  Any thoughts? Thanks in advance, PL

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to load new courses using LMB 2.5.1
ResponsesInList.Text: You've found the Achilles heel of the LMB import. Or at least one them (The other is that you cannot manually remove an enrollment that has been done with LMB). Here's what is happening (or at least what I understand is going on). The LMB importer script can run either as a separate cron job or as part of the system cron. If it's run with the moodle system cron it gets called every 15 minutes (or whatever interval that is set up to be). So there has to be some mechanism to say "this has already been processed, don't do it again". That mechanism is basically that the importer reads the xml file and makes a note of the date & time at the top: <properties lang="en"> <datasource>INB Banner</datasource> <datetime>2013-08-16T11:14:36</datetime> </properties> If you try to run the same file again, in this case at a time after 11:14, it'll just skip the whole thing thinking that it's already been run and you get the laconic message 'import log <blank> will appear below' because nothing has been imported. The solution now is obvious. Just change the time or date in the <datetime> field to a later time or date and the file  will now process properly. This is something that only happens when you're testing and believe me, it took me a long time to get to the bottom of what was going on! Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: ldap enrolment plugin limited to 1000 courses
ResponsesInList.Text: We are using a variation of the ldap enrolment module to populate rosters and have run into an issue.  When we have more than 1000 courses in our OU the ldap_get_entries call doesn't get them all.  There is a 1000 entry limit on that function in php.  I'm working on a way around this, but wanted to see if anyone else has run into this issue and has a workaround. Thanks, Nate Baxley

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ldap enrolment plugin limited to 1000 courses
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Nate, the limit is not in the php function, but on the server side. In order to keep resources under reasonable levels, the server puts a limit on the number of results it returns. 1000 is the usual limit with MS Active Directory. In order to deal with more entries than the server limit, you need to use LDAP Paged Results, which aren't supported until PHP 5.4. If you have PHP 5.4 or later, and you have Moodle 2.4 or later (which includes MDL-36119 , but be sure to use a recent version of 2.4 that includes the fix for MDL-37315 ) you can used LDAP Paged Results. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Uploading users: the Upload type option
ResponsesInList.Text: In uploading users, there are four options for Upload type. The help says this: ----------------- Updating existing accounts By default Moodle adds new user accounts and skips existing users lines where the `username` matches an existing account. Set "Upload Type" to Add new and update existing users , and existing user account will be updated. Add all, append number to usernames if needed Add new and update existing users Update existing users only Warning : errors updating existing accounts can affect your users badly. Be careful when using the options to update" --------------- What exactly does the "Add new and update existing users do? --------------- There are two constraints: no duplicate usernames (obviously) and no duplicate addresses. (A system setting I believe) What I think I want to happen: Look at the email. If it is a duplicate, then do nothing (except if there is a request to add user to a course, to do so)  ie we have assumed there is a user there, and they have a unique address, and just keep them on the books.  But don't create another account, don't change the username. Look next at usernames. If it is a duplicate username, but a unique address not already in the system, then it is to create a username+digit and proceed. And to flag it to me.  This means there MAY be a problem with one person with two accounts and different emails.  I can live with this. I now have a situation where Iget everything.  Duplicate usernames, duplicate emails, etc etc. -Derek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group enrollment prompt does not appear
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok.. 1. In Site admin>Plugins>  Enrolment>Manage enrol plugins make sure that manual enrolment and self enrolment are enabled 2. Click the Settings link for manual enrolment (which you see from the above link in #1) and make sure it is  added to new courses by default. That way, when you make a new course you won't need to add manual enrolment as a plugin as it will already have been enabled. 3. Click the Settings link for self enrolment (which you see from the above link in #1) and do the same. Also on this page is where you can set it to use course enrolment keys by default and group enrolment keys by default (if you need that in ALL your courses) Then when you go to a course you will have to specify what you want for the course as a course key and a group key. 4. Make a brand new course with nobody in it. 5. In course administration>Users>Enrolment methods, make sure manual and self enrolment are enabled. 6. Click the configuration icon for self enrolment and add a key for the course (which can be anything) and then set group enrolment key to "yes" if not already done. 7. In Course administration>Users>Groups, make a group and add a group enrolment key. 8. Test it with a  real (test) student account of a  user who does not have access elsewhere on Moodle and do not test with "switch role to" or "log in as" 9. Type the group enrolment key in. (If you type the course enrolment key you will get into the course but you will not be in the group.)

ResponsesInList.Text: I've solved this one, so am documenting it. Firstly my description is wrong above. The "Manager" role does work. I has cloned this role and was using the new cloned role when trying it. The issue was that when cloning or duplicating a role, its overrides are not cloned at the same time. Within the new role you need to Allow role overrides on appropriate levels Site administration / ▶ Users / ▶ Permissions / ▶ Define roles and click on the tab Allow role overrides. I clicked on everything from Teacher down to Authenticated user on front page and this worked. I then removed unnecessary control privileges for this new role.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group enrollment limitation
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Whitney, It can be done by using Cohort feature of Moodle. What you have to do are: Create a Cohort. Assign users in that Cohort as Student role Enroll the users in your Course by clicking on Enrol Cohort tabs which you will find in Course Administration> Users>Enrolled Users Now when you click on Enroll Cohort tab you will get a small pop-up window in which you will find two tabs "enroll users" and "enroll cohort". Please click on Enroll users tab, don't click on enroll cohort tab. Now the users will be enrolled as Manual Enrollment. So now make some settings in Manual enrollment method which you will find under Course administration>Users>Enrollment Methods> Manual Enrollment. Set Default enrollment duration to your requirement. Also set the "Enrollment expiration action" to "un-enrol users from course" which you will find in Site administration>Plugins>Enrollment>Manual enrollment. I hope this will help you. Thanks, S.Kavita

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Email students on enrollment
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Tony, My understanding (and hopefully more experienced Moodlers will correct me if I'm wrong) is that Moodle 2 does not automatically email students who have been manually enrolled.  While this is inconvenient at times, you can workaround it by using the Participants list. Within your course, go to Navigation block -> Course short name -> Participants.  From here, you can select all those students in your course who have not yet logged into your course, and send them a message, letting them know they've been enrolled.  It works best when your site administrator has forced users to receive email notifications of Personal Messages between users, to make sure the student receives the message in their email inbox (in case they have not yet been on the Moodle site). For more on this, you can see the docs link here: http://docs.moodle.org/25/en/Participants Or for a walk through, you can watch the video here: I hope this helps! Happy Moodling! Lindy @moodlechick

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk / automated course creation with phpMyAdmin
ResponsesInList.Text: With our mass course creation, similar to yours but using direct db queries from an external machine, we ignore the modinfo and let moodle fill that in.  So far so good for us.  But the blockinfo determines what blocks you want to show up and where by default -- very handy! Remember each block has a unique id in mdl_blocks.  In ours activity_modules is id=1, course_list is id=5 and online_users is id=9 for example.  Say you want the first two on the left and the third on the right for all of your autogenerated courses.  In that case, blockinfo = "1,5:9" .  block ids to the left of the colon show up on the left, the right on the right. I'm not sure about the sortorder.  I wound up finding the highest current value in the table and incrementing by 1 for each course.  I suspect these are updated when you sort courses when browsing your categories. --S

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk / automated course creation with phpMyAdmin
ResponsesInList.Text: It looks like 1.5 has a new way of configuring blocks on pages.  It's pretty slick. The block info is now stored in a new table called mdl_block_instance with 9 fields: id = unique table index blockid  = the unique id of the block from mdl_block pageid = essentially the unique course id where the block is pagetype = I think this is for blocks showing up on a course page vs module page.  All of mine say course-view. position = left (l) or right (r) ? weight = 3 is lower on the page than a 2.  It's an ordering, 0 is a the top of the page side. visible = 1 -> yes, 0 -> no configdata = must for be for blocks that need to save some configuration data. I found that creating a course in 1.5 via direct database SQL as I did in 1.4 yields a course with no blocks.  Inserting rows to mdl_block_instance adds the blocks I want to the course in the location I want. Nicely modular.  It was a good idea to strip the block display out of the course data since modules can have blocks now. Hopefully this will help.  Now I have to update my routines to do this. --S

Students will then get the message "Manual enrolments are disabled" when they try and enrol themselves. We've set our courses up to completely prevent guest/read-only access as well for non-enrolled students; this can be done by setting the value of "guest" to 0 in your CSV file for all courses. ResponsesInList.Title: Svar: External database authentication Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: This is standard behavior for the external enrolment method. Moodle checks the external database for the user that try to log in, and if exist: Moodle create a Moodle account for this user on the fly. This Moodle user account is connected to the external enrollment method, so Moodle will always check the external database in future logins. I advice you to add the "autoenroll cohort" plugin so all of these users automatically are added to a cohort. Then you set up a cohort sync as a course enrollment method and you are done. When the user log in for the first time, he/she is added to the cohort and have access to courses directly. Have a look at that plugin. Regards Alf Martin

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Newbie Enrolment questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dominic, All of us were newbies at one time or other, so there should no embarrassment in being one. One thing it took me a while to get my head around with Moodle is this important idea: the ONLY role that applies across the whole Moodle is "Administrator". Every other role is assigned at the course or activity level. Examples: at the College where I work, we have some "courses" used for administrative purposes where the Faculty members are "Students" within those "courses". In other "courses", some members of the student body of the College have the role of "Teacher". We also have both Undergraduate and Postgraduate students, and some Postgraduate students help with teaching in Undergraduate courses, so they are Students in their allocated Postgrad subjects and Teachers (or Non-Editing Teachers) in the Undergrad subjects they are teaching in. Likewise, some of the upper-year Undergrad students tutor in first-year undergrad subjects, so have the same kind of mixed access. Once you get your head around the "only Admins have a site-wide role", you can then plan how you handle everything else. That doesn't answer the questions you ask, but I hope it helps you understand the parameters of the system. HTH Rob

I hope i am right and not leading y ou on a wild goose chase.

ResponsesInList.Title: Merging multiple accounts?
ResponsesInList.Text: Does anyone know if there is a way of taking two user accounts and merging them into one? The problem I'm having is there are several students who created themselves an account to take a course. Then, they couldn't remember their login the next time they came back to take another course so they created a new account.  So now I have users with two accounts, one showing completion of one course, and another showing the completion of other courses. We need them to have just one account with all their course completions in them. We're running moodle 2.4. Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Merging multiple accounts?
ResponsesInList.Text:
That's a really difficult question. While it is technically possible to do it, it's quite complicated and error-prone. You would need to modify Moodle's database directly in a lot of places, which is quite risky unless you know the database structure very well. There are two ways Moodle refers to a users: by their usernames (which is only used in very few places, like the user list table, the logs table, and probably one or two other places), by their internal numeric IDs (which is used almost everywhere). This is where you should put all your efforts. You would need to modify every single table that references the internal ID and change if from the soon-to-be-discarded-ID to the want-to-keep-user-ID. Of course this means you should already know which those tables are, which depending on your Moodle version and the contributed plugins you have installed can vary quite a bit. As I said before, while technically possible, it's not trivial at all. Oh, and by the way, don't even try to do anything like this before having full backups of your Moodle database and having restored them at least once (so you know you can recover when you screw up your database). Saludos.
Iñaki.

As Mary says, that setting is actually for what you are looking for.... under the right conditions It only works in 2.x, and only for the 'traditional' user enrolment screen. If you want to make it work in the new AJAX user selector (the one used by default), you have to modify a javascript file a bit. In Moodle 2.0.x, in addition to using the setting Mary mentions, you need to modify enrol/yui/enrolmentmanager/enrolmentmanager.js around line 345, and change the lines that read: ```text .append(Y.Node.create('
') .append(Y.Node.create('
'+user.fullname+'
')) .append(Y.Node.create('
'+user.email+'
'))) ``` to read: ```text .append(Y.Node.create('
') .append(Y.Node.create('
'+user.fullname+'
')) .append(Y.Node.create('
'+user.email+'
')) .append(Y.Node.create('
'+user.username+'
'))) ``` In Moodle 2.1.x, you need to modify /enrol/manual/yui/quickenrolment/quickenrolment.js around line 347, and change the lines as above. In Moodle 1.9.x (what you are using), you need to edit file /admin/roles/assign.html, around line 78, and change the line that reads: ```text echo "id\">".$fullname.", ".$user->email."\n"; ``` to read: ```text echo "id\">".$fullname.", ".$user->email.", ".$user->username."\n"; ``` you also need to edit file /admin/roles/assign.php around line 328 and change the line that reads: ```text $select = " SELECT DISTINCT u.id, u.firstname, u.lastname, u.email"; ``` to read: ```text $select = " SELECT DISTINCT u.id, u.username, u.firstname, u.lastname, u.email"; ``` and the same file around line 362 to change the lines that reads: ```text $availableusers = get_recordset_ sql ('SELECT id, firstname, lastname, email ``` to read: ```text $availableusers = get_recordset_sql('SELECT id, username, firstname, lastname, email ``` That should do the trick Saludos. Iñaki.

A login-time lookup is performed against the external database. An easy way of checking how it's working is to try logging in as a student. In Moodle 1.6 I used to use the "Login as" button on a student's profile page to prompt a login-time lookup. External database enrolment also manages unenrolment. Yes, this does this mean that a student who is not in the database any more is removed from the course (again only tried in Moodle 1.6). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Someone explain external database enrolment, please??
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been there and fought that battle. External database enrollment simply means that Moodle will read an external database (via ADODB) to determine enrollments for roles in courses. This is generally managed by view in your database containing your student records. The contents of this view are compared against Moodle's own role assignment tables, and from these contents, Moodle's tables are updated. Moodle connects to the external database for this comparison both 1) when a user logs into Moodle, and 2) whenever the moodle/enrol/database/enrol_database_sync.php script is run (usually in a cron job). This script synchronizes all enrollments for all users. I would disagree about the usefulness of logging in as a student to test the process... particularly when using a secure authentication connection such as LDAP where the admin doesn't know the login info! Manually run the enrol_database_sync.php script to see the process run. Unenrollment occurs when the student's role assignment no longer exists in the external database. If you really want to keep your role assignments permanently, that's fine... just keep the assignment in the external database view (or perhaps better, set up a "guest" style historical role in Moodle, and have your external database move folks to that new role after the class is over.) If a course doesn't exist in Moodle which is referenced in your external database, the script will (buggishly, but I think this has been reported and fixed in later versions) report that as a notice. Alternately, if you have the settings configured to automatically create the course, the script will take the (optional) template course and copy it into the specified category as a new course for the associated enrollments. I don't recommend it... it's inflexible and course creation doesn't belong in the context of enrollments. Create the necessary courses beforehand (we use a script to connect to another view in the database). Hope that helps a bit.

So if a user never logs in, s/he is never enrolled into any course (by the external database enrolment plugin). I do get a few irritating notices about skipping courses at the top of the screen but that looks like a bug. I'd say this is a bug too. If you have everything correctly setup, the user should log in normally and see the list of courses s/he is enrolled into, just as you'd be using manual enrolment. At least that's what we get in our setup. Next sentence - "External database enrolment also manages unenrolment. ". This worries me! What exactly does this mean? Does this mean that a student who is not in the database (any more) will be removed from the course? If so, is there any way to stop this? I am thinking about completed courses that I want to keep available in an "archive". It means that if a given user is no longer in the external enrolment database, as far as Moodle concerns, this user is no longer enrolled into any courses. The external database is the master for the enrolment data, so Moodle just 'synchronizes' to that data. If you don't want your users to be unenrolled, you need to remove the part of the code that unenrols people, or mark those enrolmentes that you want to 'archive' as 'manual' enrolments (so the external database enrolment plugins doesn't touch them). Next para. "You may synchronize all enrolments by executing the enrol_database_sync.php script". Ok, what does that do? Errr..... never mind This is quite understandable. If you are going to enrol someone into a course, you need that someone to exist in Moodle beforehand. As users are created the first time they log in, unless you synchronize your users (to create/delete all of them without having to log in), there'll be no users to enrol. A bit convoluted, but completely logical Elsewhere in the forum , automatic course generation gets mentioned, but I don't see any reference to this. How does this work - if it indeed exists? It exists (we are using it too ). If you enable course creation, whenever the plugin tries to enrol someone into a course, it checks whether the course exists or not. If it doesn't, it pulls some data from your external enrolment database and creates the course on the fly, and then enrols that someone into the course. You can configure a couple of things or two (like the course template for course auto-creation and the category where you are going to put your course), but that's it in standard Moodle. We have a little patch that adds some additional settings like being able to specify a differente category and template for each course (available for 1.5 through 1.9dev). Should you be interested in it, you can get it from: http://orodruin.escomposlinux.org/~iarenaza/moodle/ (there is no 1.9 directory there because there is no 1.9 version yet, but the patch for 1.8 applies cleanly to 1.9dev as of today). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Someone explain external database enrolment, please??
ResponsesInList.Text: So if I manually add a student to a course and they are not mentioned in the database they will be removed again when they next log in? No, they won't (thankfully ). Moodle tracks the enrolment 'origin' of every enrolment (from 1.5 on at least). So the external database enrolment plugin only 'plays' with enrolments marked with 'database' origin. You can mix-and-match enrolments from different plugins at the same time on the same course from 1.6 on, and every sub-system will only touch its. Expanding on my removing users question, what happens if I subsequently remove the id number from the course settings, so it can no longer match up with the external database - do all the students then stay regardless of their status in the external database or do they all get thrown out. If the enrolment is marked as 'database' and Moodle can no longer find the course in the external database, then it's removed. You need to change those enrolments to 'manual' (for example) to make them stay. Another question - does "login as" a user run the database lookup (as the docs rather imply), as opposed to actually logging in as a student. With 1.6, it did. With the new roles thing, I don't really know (have never tried myself). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Someone explain external database enrolment, please??
ResponsesInList.Text: Sophia, We use custom .php scripts to "freeze" the enrolments at the end of each term.  This is accomplished by updating the moodle database's mdl_enrol_assignments table setting the enrol field to "manual".  This will prevent an enrolment from dropping if we no longer have it in an external database.  I can share our .php script if you feel you need more information.  So our process is the following: We name our courses starting with the term (e.g. FA-10_MW4103_A) which then populates that name in the shortname, fullname, and idnumber fields during the external db synch.  The teachers can edit the short and full names later. As we reach the end of the current term, we run the script that changes the enrol field value from "database" to "manual".  This prevents the student's enrolment from dropping when we no longer have it in the external db. At the start of the next term, we run the script to "hide" enrolments from students by updating the visible field value to 0 in the mdl_course table of the moodle db.  It's our policy to not allow students to access past resources after the following term starts. I hope this helps and please let me know if you want a copy of our .php script. Sincerely, Dave Kendall

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Someone explain external database enrolment, please??
ResponsesInList.Text: Sophia, We have automated the process by creating a function in our SIS's SQL server that returns the start and end dates of our terms and using it in our custom .php scripts.  Those scripts are part of the scheduled task that runs the external database synchronization.  The custom script compares the results of the function to the current date and performs the appropriate 'freeze" or "hide" depending on whether it's the last day of the current term or the day before the start of the next term. As for informing the external database of marks, completion dates, etc, we have not done that so I can't offer any help through experience on that.  I would assume that if your techs know how to extract and import data into MySQL, that someone could figure it out. ResponsesInList.Title: Help with Manual Enrolments
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, We are shortly due to upgrade to Moodle 2 and are creating our site from scratch so that we lose any old data etc from our 1.9 site that we do not need anymore. We are a Local Authority and would like all of our staff to be automatically enrolled onto all of our courses. We also have external delegates who need to view maybe one or two courses (these can be different courses) and so want to stop the external delegates being able to view all of the other courses. I understand if I leave all courses with manual enrolment as the default setting, no students will be able to enrol onto any courses on their own. This is fine for the external delegates, but is there a way of easily enrolling all of our staff onto all of the courses (we have around 70 courses)? Thanks in advance, Lauren.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help with Manual Enrolments
ResponsesInList.Text: I am not sure what you would class as "easily enrolling" but you  could use a csv file - see Upload_users with, for example username, password,email,firstname,lastname,course1,course2, course3 etc etc where course1 and so on are the  short names of all the courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help with Manual Enrolments
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd suggest creating a system-wide cohort for your staff.  Then it is easy to add that cohort to your classes as an enrolment method.  This is a bit safer than giving everyone a site-wide or category level role, and easy to manage when you add or lose a staff member.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help with Manual Enrolments
ResponsesInList.Text: The only issue with cohorts is that the cohort has to be manually added by admin to each course -whereas csv upload will add them in the course automatically. On the other hand, cohorts would as Chad says make your life a lot easier when staff come and go as the cohort would sync enrolments once they have been set up -whereas csv would not.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to remove students using csv files

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mark, A word of caution with groups and existing work - I have run into problems with this in the past in terms of having students in more than one group on a course page;  I think switching students around groups AFTER work has been input by those students will cause disruption. It seems likely that work is permanently coded to a student and group based on the group that the student is in when they first submit.  If the student is in more than one group, the work seems to be assigned to the first group that shows up in the list. Hence, the work may not be visible if you look  at the student through a different group, and if you change the groups completely the student seems to lose access to the group. This is counter-intuitive to me as I would expect ALL work to be coded to the student, with the question of the group then being addresses through a look up table. I don't see why a student (and their work) should not be visible in any number of groups that they are attached to (which seems to be the case with groupings). regards Paul

For instance, last year, we ran a one-day Performance Management class that was required for all of our managers.  We did 18 classes (same content, same trainer) for 18 different groups of people, and people were able to choose which date they wanted to sign up for. Within Moodle, I'd like to have the ability to: Give people options to sign up for the various face-to-face session and send out email confirmations, etc. (F2F plug-in is installed) Take attendance (Attendance plug-in installed) for each session that we offer Require this course for all managers, but still give them the option of which dates they want to attend. Should I create a new Course for every new group of people who will attend? Or do I create one Course (Performance Management) and then within that do several F2F modules and Attendance modules. Should I manually Enroll all the managers as a Group (or Cohort?) into the Performance Management Course, and then within the course they can select the dates of the F2F sessions that work best for them? Any assistance people can provide in helping me to set this up in the most logical way possible, would be SO greatly appreciated. Thank you! Stephanie

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrollment, Face-to-Face, Attendance, Groups, Cohorts...
ResponsesInList.Text: If it were me, I'd set up a single course for Performance Management. Within that course, I'd use the Group Self-Selection module to allow the users to select their own groups. Each group would be for a particular F2F date. I've never used cohorts before, but from what I've read, it would be a good way to quickly enroll certain types of employees (such as managers) at the same time. But that idea might break down if some employees would be members of more than one cohort, such as a Managers cohort and an IT department cohort. I'm not sure if Moodle allows users to be in more than one cohort. HTH , Kimber

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Paypal - Monthly Subsciptions 2.1.1
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not sure if you got this resolved, but I just posted this to the forum: I wanted to be able to convert a course over to Moodle for a small business and they have a subscription AND trial period for their product. Here's what I did to get most of it to work. In the file: moodle/enrol/paypal/enrol.html I added these tags: Replaced: <input type="hidden" name="cmd" value="_xclick" /> with: <input type="hidden" name="cmd" value="_xclick-subscriptions" /> Added the lines below based on the PayPal document: https://cms.paypal.com/cms_content/US/en_US/files/developer/PP_WebsitePaymentsStandard_IntegrationGuide.pdf The $0.00 trial period doesn't work because if you set a course to $0.00, it doesn't redirect to PayPal (since there is no charge for it). Another chicken and egg problem is that the subscription code, below, worked (redirected me to PayPal) because I set the course to cost $9.99 via the PayPal module in Moodle. However, if I set the trial-period cost to $0.00, the PayPal subscription completes, but the redirect back to Moodle still shows $0.00 was paid so the student doesn't get enrolled into the course. We had to change the model to require a $9.99 payment up front, which they can cancel after 7 days, if they wanted. After the subscription is processed, the PayPal message errors, BUT when they click the button "Return to Course page" from the PayPal window, they get enrolled into the course. <!-- Trial period --> <!-- Pay $9.99 (a1) during a 30 (p1) Day (t1) trial period --> <input type="hidden" name="a1" value="9.99"> <input type="hidden" name="p1" value="30"> <input type="hidden" name="t1" value="D"> <!-- This is a hack because the customer can ask for a refund at the end of the 7 days (we have to advertise that though). --> <!-- Regular Time period charge $9.99 (a3) each (p3) month (t3) --> <input type="hidden" name="a3" value="9.99"> <input type="hidden" name="p3" value="1"> <input type="hidden" name="t3" value="M"> <!-- NOTE: This must be set to a3, p3, t3, etc. --> <!-- PayPal has an a2, p2, t2, etc. option to allow secondary trial periods (see document link above) We don't use that so we skip over those settings. --> <!-- Charge until customer cancels (via their PayPal account) or the PayPal account holder for our business cancels the subscription --> <input type="hidden" name="src" value="1"> All together without all the extra text: <!-- Enable subscription --> <input type="hidden" name="cmd" value="_xclick-subscriptions" /> <!-- Trial period --> <input type="hidden" name="a1" value="9.99"> <input type="hidden" name="p1" value="30"> <input type="hidden" name="t1" value="D"> <!-- Regular Time period charge --> <input type="hidden" name="a3" value="9.99"> <input type="hidden" name="p3" value="1"> <input type="hidden" name="t3" value="M"> <!-- Charge until it is canceled --> <input type="hidden" name="src" value="1"> Maybe the PayPal module developers could include options for this in the future. Just thought I'd share what worked for me. NOTE: It doesn't appear the enrol.html file changes on a regular basis, but for each upgrade of Moodle, I have a backup copy of my manual changes so I can add back after the upgrade.

ResponsesInList.Title: Custom group welcome email upon enrolling
ResponsesInList.Text: Wondering how I can set custom welcome email that depends on which group they enroll into...is there a placeholder for this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Custom group welcome email upon enrolling
ResponsesInList.Text: Write a local event trapping function for event 'groups_member_added' Your handler will receive as parameter an object with two fields (groupid and userid). userid is the id of the user just enroled in table mdl_user groupid is the id of a record in table mdl_group from which you can retrieve the target group  to personnalize the mail. Within your handler function, do all testing/querying you want with these fields...and finally call Moodle function email_to_user() For details see http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Events_API http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Local_plugins and http://xref.moodle.org/nav.html?_functions/index.html Cheers

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Phil, I think I found a way that works.  I'm using moodle 2.0.2.  This seems to work on my test server and a production server.   I add the enrollment to the confirmation step as I believe the user needs to be confirmed before they can be enrolled. in auth/email/auth.php add the following to function user_confirm, about line 136, right before return AUTH_CONFIRM_OK; // get libraries require_once($CFG->libdir.'/enrollib.php'); // get plugin $plugin = enrol_get_plugin('manual'); // id of course signups should be in $targetcourseid = 5; // create instance $enrolperson = $DB -> get_record('enrol',array('courseid'=>$targetcourseid,'enrol'=>'manual')); // do enrollment $plugin->enrol_user($enrolperson,$user->id,$targetcourseid); you will also need to add $CFG to the globals for user_confirm i.e. global $DB,$CFG;

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cohort sync enrolled users still remain while moving course from one category to another category
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, cohort sync is not hard-linked to categories, there is an artificial restriction that you can use only cohorts from system or parent categories when setting up new cohort sync. It is safe to move the courses around, the cohorts will be kept in sync. If you want to remove some cohort sync delete it from the list of course enrolment methods. Alternatively if you want to keep users in groups and do not want to loose all grades, etc. you can just disable the cohort sync. Petr

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External Database not working.
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, solved it.  PowerCampus only puts out uppercase designators for the roles (FAC, STUD).  Moodle only takes lowercase.  You could alter core files into accepting uppercase when checking for a match, but that could easily be wiped out the next time you update moodle.  I got around it by exporting the tables from PowerCampus, running a little 'sed' magic over them, then importing them into moodle's my sql database and reading from that as the 'external' database. Time to go see if there is a tracker bug on this case sensitivity issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.x and PayPal Enrolment
ResponsesInList.Text: We found the problem in our case. The first discovery of note is that the ipn.php file is not sending out error messages via email, as it is designed to do. We are looking further into that. What was causing the problem in our situation was a case mismatch in the email settings in Moodle and PayPal. Normally email addresses are not case sensitive, but the ipn.php file compares the strings and if they do not exactly match (including case) the enrollment fails, and no error message is sent. So Joe@domain.com ≠ joe@ domain .com. I have edited the documentation wiki to reflect the above so others don't waste their time. If we locate the problem in the error reporting and fix it we will submit the code. Otherwise we'll report the bug in the tracking system. I think that why so many people have problems with this enrollment plugin is due to the lack or informative error messages. Hope this helps you resolve your issue as well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.x and PayPal Enrolment
ResponsesInList.Text: We have identified the bug in the ipn.php file that failed to send error messages and have submitted the revised and debugged code to the Moodle core developers, so hopefully it will be pushed out in a Moodle update soon.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.x and PayPal Enrolment
ResponsesInList.Text: John, may I ask how you submitted the fix? I want to see whether you found the same thing I've just found. 've run into this problem and spend time debugging it too. The problem I found was that ipn.php tries to access the non-ssl version of Paypal, so it gets a redirect from Paypal: HTTP/1.0 302 Found Location: https://www.sandbox.paypal.com Server: BigIP Connection: close Content-Length: 0 (I'm testing with a sandbox, and of course the redirect was never followed.) To fix it, I just need to change the connection URL to use ssl:// I'm attaching a patch in case it may help. I hope this will be fixed in upstream Moodle soon.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Paypal functionality does not work
ResponsesInList.Text: If the web server call to paypal.com is being blocked (such is case with many shared hosting providers) then you may be able to route via a proxy server. Unfortunately, the current version of moodle uses fsockopen which does not readily support proxy servers. I have made a patch (attached) which essentially replaces the current fsockopen and fputs with curl configured to use a proxy server. The actual proxy serveraddress and port number will need be customised before using - this should really be set via the plugin's configuration page but didn't really have the time. Anyway, the patch was made against moodle 1.9.5.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PayPal IPN Address
ResponsesInList.Text: A number of points or answers to your questions... Ideally you should ignore the PayPal Sandbox and use live PayPal. You can always refund yourself so you will not lose money. Not using the sandbox makes things simpler and there are some indications that the sandbox does not work as well as the real PayPal and has caused people problems. If you must use the sandbox, edit the file config.php in the Moodle root and add the line "$CFG->usepaypalsandbox = 1;" before the require_once(...) line. This one change will allow you to avoid editing the two other files. To answer "How do I set the PayPal addresses in the enrolment plug-in to the business address of my sandbox acct?"... Log in as moodle Administrator and go to Site Administration... Courses... Enrolments... Select Edit for PayPal. The email address of your business PayPal account is set on that page (along with other stuff). When you save you must make sure that on the page you return to that you click the checkbox to Enable PayPal and also probably set it as the Default and then press Save changes. (you do NOT change these in either "the original log in account I have with sandbox or the business test account?" as you suggest.) You should not have to set the IPN address anywhere. This is passed by Moodle so you do not have to set it in PayPal. (If you were to set it in PayPal for some reason it would be http://paganstudies.eduspoke.com/enrol/paypal/ipn.php .) To answer, "How do I remove the .sandbox references from what files?"... Assuming you have set the setting in config.php as above (and I suggest you do not), then just take out that line. If the above does not work for you, I am willing to help you more if you wish. You might want to give me admin access to you moodle and send me your PayPal business account e-mail address. You can send this to alanabarrett0 AT gmail.com. Hopefully, though you will be able to get it to work on your own. Alan.

Also make sure that your Paypal account IPN is set to use UTF8. So rule 1 No aliases or redirects rule 2 UTF8 character encoding.

Once the student has gone through official channels and made it into the course, the flatfile changes to add the "student" role and remove the "waitlist" role for that student.  However, what happens is that after the "student" role is added, when "waitlist" is removed, it actually removes the student completely from the course (i.e. NO roles at all).  So instead of just removing "waitlist", the code actually removes "student" as well. We have a workaround that pretty much works, in which we remove the "waitlist" role and then add the "student" role (we changed the order).  Still, we thought this problem might affect others - sometimes there's a case when a person has more than one role in a course, and if you want to remove just one of the multiple roles with a flatfile but keep the others, you just plain can't.  ALL of the person's roles are deleted instead of just the one you want, and they are then completely cut off from seeing the course. edit: version is 2.3.2!

ResponsesInList.Title: Integration of a full featured "Subscription" Program
ResponsesInList.Text: Fellow Moodlers, I am a newbie to Moodling and am learning more by the day! I currently deliver training on a discussion forum based site by controlling access to specific forums. The forum control is handled by a neat subscription script called aMember. aMember will work with over 30 payment processors and is available with over 20 integration "plug-ins" (such as Invision Power board, VBulliten, Mambo, etc). I am in the process of changing my site over to a Moodle site. The only thing I need is better ecommerce. Moodlers do a good job of developing the educational functionality, but not so well on the ecommerce side. The subscription software business is a specialized business. It requires an intimate knowledge about how the different payment processors work and how each one handles recurring billing. It also has to handle subscription periods, renewal notices, recurring subscription periods, etc. This is where aMember really shines. They do this well! If Alex (the main man at aMember) would write a plug-in for Moodle, this is some of the functionality it would add. 1. Subscribe students to the same course for different lengths of time. 2. The ability for a student to purchase multiple courses in one transaction. 3. The ability to have a course subscription be billed on a recurring basis. 3. Choose from over 30 payment processors 4. The ability to offer downloads for a fee. 5. Generate coupons that could be redeemed at checkout. 6. Implementation of an affiliate program. 7. And much much more.... aMember is not open source. The program is $140 and most of his plug-ins run about $40. I have made a post on his site asking that he look into writing a Moodle plug-in. While it would cost close to $180 to implement, this could be quickly recouped on a business site. Take a look at http://www.amember.com/ My post asking Alex to consider writing a plug-in is here http://www.amember.com/forum/showthread.php?goto=newpost&t=2755 Another option is if for someone else to write the plug in. This is above my technical abilities! Alex provides information on how to do this in this manual: http://www.amember.com/docs/aMember.pdf The information is on pages 60-63. In summary this is not a ad for aMember. I have used aMember's subscription scripts for years on another project and have found the program and Alex at aMember to be top notch. I think Moodle integrated with aMember would be a great product for the business users. My hopes are that aMember will develop the plug-in and make it available on their site. If others are interested, it would not hurt to go register with aMembers forum and let Alex know that I am not alone I have also submitted a ticket to aMember support requesting a quote on writing this plug-in if aMember does not put it on its development calendar. I will do this as a custom programming job if this is what it takes. I will report back the status of this plug-in as soon as I hear anything! Grant Swaim

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Integration of a full featured "Subscription" Program
ResponsesInList.Text: Craig, It will definitely handle your RORO scenario and more. aMember is a php/ mySql application that is a subscription manager. It is a stand alone application that Moodle would query for user authentication and class enrollment information. An administrator would set up all the classes in aMember as products. All the products have a duration (definable in days months or years). For instance Math 101 could be in the product list multiple times with different subscription durations (30 days access, 3 months access, 1 years access, etc). When a student purchases a class they are directly accessing the aMember program. They pick out the classes they want to purchase, they then check out using the payment processor you chose (from a list of +30) You can actually give them the option of more than one, such as PayPal and 2CheckOut. The credit card transaction is handled in real time and if the transaction is successful they aMember database will reflect they are members in the classes they paid for and for the length of times for the separate classes. At each log-in Moodle would check the aMember database to see which classes the student holds a current subscription in. There is definitely a learning curve because aMember has so many configurable features. My plan is to get this working and then write detailed instructions on how to integrate aMember and Moodle. I hope to have this all finished within a couple of weeks. Grant

ResponsesInList.Text: N. Hansen, I can appreciate your point of view. I also understand that using commercial software to accomplish these goals runs against the open source philosophy. I am a newbie here and after hours and hours of reading information on this site I came to the following conclusions: Moodle is a great platform to deliver elearning! Moodle does not have the necessary ecommerce capabilities to suit my needs. For me to use Moodle I need more ecommerce features. Based on forum posts, there seems to be a lot of business users that want more features too, such as: more payment processor options, the ability to automatically enroll and unenroll students in classes, the ability to implement an affiliate program, the ability to generate coupons, etc. After looking at the dates of the forum posts requesting more ecommerce and the responses, I came to the conclusion that additional ecommerce functionality is not on any body's short list. First of all, I am not a programmer; however, I have a theory about why advanced ecommerce functionality has not been programmed by the Moodle programming community. so if I am way off base here one of you programmers let me know The group of programmers that work on Moodle projects do a great job of writing modules to deliver content. Nobody does it better! However, It appears to me that programming ecommerce features is a lot different than programming elearning delivery modules. It seems to be a specialty business, just like Moodle specializes in elearning. Actually there are only a few companies that offer "subscription / membership" management software. Keep in mind that this type of software is very different than a typical shopping cart program. A good subscription script, such as aMember, will take into consideration the following functions / features. The ability to handle real time credit card transactions with a large choice of payment processors. This requires that they have an intimate knowledge of how each payment processor handles instant payment notification (IPN) and recurring charges. The ability to sell products with a set duration along with all the variations of this, such as: What do you do if someone purchases an additional subscription to a course before the current subscription is complete. Do you have the subscriptions overlap or have the new superscription start at the end of the current one. The ability to make subscriptions conditional such as, you cannot subscribe to Math 102 until your subscription to Math 101 has ended. The ability to send pre-written email notices to students x-number of days after they have enrolled for a class. The ability to send an email notice x-number of days before their subscription to a course ends in case they want to rejoin the class. The ability to send bulk email to students that are enrolled in specific classes. The ability to generate "coupons" that could be used at checkout. Some of the variable of the coupon would be: A set beginning time and ending time Set up to give a discount based on percentages or a flat dollar amount Set up to only be valid with certain classes. Set up to be used X-number of times by the same user Set up to be used X-number of times with any user The ability of a student to log in a view their payment history and see the effective dates of their current subscriptions. An admin control panel that tracks every student and class with advanced reporting. The ability to implement an affiliate program that can pay based on a percentage or flat fee. That can pay on primary and secondary purchases. The list could go on, but I will stop here... In Summary In my humble opinion, to get this type of ecommerce functionality anytime soon it is going to require using a commercial product, such as aMember. True this approach is not for everybody. But in many cases, such as myself, I would not be able to use Moodle without these additional features. True this approach is going to cost approximately $140 to implement, but for many business applications this expense could be recouped rather quickly. Again, let me say i have no relationship with aMember other than I am currently using their script to control membership to a discussion based website. I have found their script to work flawlessly and their support to be first class. You can visit their site at http://www.amember.com at read their forum posts. Guests are free to read the support posts which is rare with most commercial software publishers. Specifically read some of the posts in the "Testimonials" forum. Also remember that I am still working on configuring Moodle to work directly with aMember (is should not require an aMember plug-in). As soon as this is done and tested, I will post the instructions in this post. At that point if you want to try this approach, you can go to aMember and download a working copy of aMember (good for 30 days) and try it for your self. Later.. Grant

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course creator allowed to change Guest access setting
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Zoran, Thanks for your feedback. It's nice to hear that you've fixed things... however senior developer and roles expert Petr has explained to me that my suggested solution is NOT the right way to solve the problem. This is because allowing the enrol/guest:config capability for the course creator role results in course creators having access to courses which they have not created. The right way is to first go to Settings > Site administration > Users > Permissions > Define roles and reset your course creator role to the default permissions, then set "Creators' role in new courses" in Settings > Site administration > Users > Permissions > User policies to 'Teacher'. Your course creator will then be enrolled as a teacher in the course they have just created and can then edit the guest access settings. If they wish, when they are done with editing the course settings, they can un-enrol themselves from the course. I've just updated the documentation Course creator role where hopefully all is explained! If you don't understand anything, please shout.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Free study module (with enrolment key) for students purchasing another...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dave, I don't think it's possible to prevent students giving the enrolment key to others, however if you find unwanted people enrolling you can always unenrol them and change the key (which would not affect any legitimately enrolled users). ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle External Course Creation Categories
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm using the external database enrolment plugin to setup automatic course creation, but I'm not understanding the behavior of the 'newcoursecategory' key. When I run the sync with the field blank then courses are automatically created in the designated default new course category 'defaultcategory'. But when I run it with a database column name from my courses table in the field I don't get any new courses created. Do the categories need to exist in Moodle before the sync or are they created? When I pre-create a category to match the course category listing in the database I still don't get courses created. Thanks in advance

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle External Course Creation Categories
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm afraid the standard external database enrolment plugin doesn't work that way with respect to course categories. It only allows you to specify an *existing* category *short name* where it will place all the newly created courses. You can't specify a different category for each course by using an column name in the external database. It's the same fixed category for all of them (the one you specify in the newcoursecategory field). If you want to be able what you want, you need to use something like the enhanced external database enrolment plugin that we have developed, available for Moodle 1.9 so far at http://orodruin.escomposlinux.org/~iarenaza/moodle/enrol_db_refactor/ We plan to upgrade it to Moodle 2.0.x in the near future too (we'll need it before next July). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle External Course Creation Categories
ResponsesInList.Text: I found that setting the new category field to a column name from the external database that contained fields to match the actual auto-incremented 'id' of the Moodle category (not the category short name) did work. In this case the external database courses are being sorted into the correct Moodle categories as long as the categories already exist and match the course id numbers coming from the external database. Although not as user friendly as using the category shortname it will work in our scenario. Is this not the correct behavior?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle External Course Creation Categories
ResponsesInList.Text: Yup, you are right! Looks like behaviour changed between Moodle 1.x and 2.0. You needed to specify a shortname in 1.x, but you need to specify the 'id' in 2.0

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External database with multiple tables
ResponsesInList.Text: Kimber, Other institutions have been able to create a 'view' on the database server to present the desired information as if it were one table.  I can't say if this will work or not in your case, but it might be an option to explore.  It should be possible to tailor the view to include only the information you want, but it does require someone with access to the databased to create the view for you.  You could do it through setting up your own MySQL database and populating a table based on constructed queries of the MSSQL system, but it is usually better to draw from the source directly where possible.  And if you do set something up on your own, expect to take on responsibility for maintaining it as well!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Delete user data after unenrollment
ResponsesInList.Text: Angel - I don't know your purpose for using Moodle, however, as a former administrator in both K-12 and higher ed, I want to offer the following cautions, particularly if your courses are used for any kind of credit such as professional growth or continuing education units, certification/recertification, test prep, etc. I can understand wanting to keep your server load low, however, if there is any potential that someone can challenge you/your company/your institution about the course quality, the work the individual did or did not do, the quality of the work, etc., you may find yourself in a position where you need to produce evidence. That said, my recommendation would be to do a course backup with all student data and logs and archive it with a meaningful name and a destroy date (eg., Course 1 - destroy March 31 2015).  If certification/recertification is involved, I'd save for at least 5 years -- maybe 7 or 10 to cover all possible timelines. Once the backup is archived, I'd then remove the course and data from the active server. Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Delete user data after unenrollment

The Quiz module doesn't do anything with that option, though, so if they are allowed a limited number of attempts at a quiz that will be a problem. For example, if it's set where they get one attempt at the quiz, that means one shot FOR LIFE, even if tey enrol in the class again three years later.  If that matters to you, if you'd like Quiz to respect the choice to not import old information, you can express your needs here: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/user.php?id=1468589&mode=discussions We have a fixed verson are the discussion is whether or not the fix should be accepted into Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to assign global user roles with external database enrolment plugin.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, this is Raul. I have set up the external database enrolment plugin and all the enrolments are being syncronized correctly except the enrolments targeted to the  top level of the moodle(courseId=1).
