ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PayPal Enrolement
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nicole, Just to clarify my post about the use of Paypal Developer Sandbox. This system works just the same as the Live Paypal site, except that you are using "dummy" merchants and buyers. The dummy buyers have their own dummy credit card details and you can make dummy purchases. Everything works with moodle just the same as the live site. The only thing that needs editing in your paypal plugin is the form action url in /paypal/enrol.html instead of: <form action="https://www.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr" method="post"> use <form action="https://www.sandbox.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr" method="post"> Signing up for a Paypal developer account is a fairly painless process, https://developer.paypal.com/cgi-bin/devscr?cmd=_home This info from the Paypal Developer site. The Sandbox is a safe testing environment where you can test PayPal features such as Website Payments, IPN, and Web Services. The Sandbox is a mirror of the real PayPal site except that real financial transactions are not made. Tips for using the Sandbox For more information, view the Sandbox User Guide Sandbox accounts are not in any way tied to your PayPal account on www.paypal.com When creating a Sandbox account, your email address attached to that account does not need to be real. It can be any email address, as long as the email address does not already exist on the Sandbox. Email from the Sandbox will never be delivered to the email address you enter. All email generated by the Sandbox is captured and displayed by the Developer Central email client . After creating a Sandbox account, you may want to confirm the email address for the sandbox user. Check the email client on Developer Central to confirm your email address. After creating a Sandbox account, you can also attach a test credit card and bank account for testing. I understand that Nicole is saying it's easy to just do small purchase amounts with your own credit card, however, this system negates the need to use your own card and for those people who dont have a credit card.....they must be out there. It's also handy for running multiple tests. Cheers Brett

ResponsesInList.Text: After one more iteration of this debugging (off line) I have found that the ODBC Driver/server combination returns Field names in UPPERCASE. Looking up the Moodle Tracker I see the following almost identical bug: http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-14553 The solution (as I read it from the tracker, but also had worked out myself) is just to have the remote field names specified in UPPERCASE. This is done in Courses->Enrolments->External Database (edit) (admin/enrol_config.php?enrol=database) and should be applied to all remote database fields: "enrol_remotecoursefield", "enrol_remoteuserfield" and "enrol_db_remoterolefield". The external database itself should not be changed. However there is an additional problem not solved by the above fix... The line "if ($rs = $enroldb->Execute("SELECT {$CFG->enrol_remotecoursefield} as enrolremotecoursefield ..." dynamically generates the field enrolremotecoursefield in upper case as ENROLREMOTECOURSEFIELD!!! So I had to add the following six lines to enrol.php... if (empty($fields_obj->enrolremotecoursefield)) { $courselist[] = $fields_obj->ENROLREMOTECOURSEFIELD; } else { $courselist[] = $fields_obj->enrolremotecoursefield; } to replace the single line... $courselist[] = $fields_obj->enrolremotecoursefield; I have sent you separately an enrol.php with this fix and still more debug info to make sure I am on the right track. After that, if the debug info shows I am on the right track, you will need to make the above external database configuration entries in UPPERCASE. Assuming that works I will give you a clean enrol.php. I will also update the tracker bug. The bug in your case also applies to a wider range of drivers... MSSQL using the ODBC driver and the ODBC_MSSQL driver ORACLE using the odbc driver and the odbc_oracle driver The move from 1.8 to 1.9 seems to have caused the wider issue and I have not been able to track down the root issue (yet). Alan.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Major bug found in 1.9 with Course->Enrolment->Database->ODBC
ResponsesInList.Text: Glad it is all sorted! Here is the text I have added to the above Moodle Tracker entry for this bug (which documents the changes in the file Lewis has attached above)... I have come up with a proper solution. Rather than work around ADODB_ASSOC_CASE having the wrong value for the ODBC connection, I have extended the above fix to temporarily UPPERCASE the Object Property names used to access the Record Object. The Property names come from $CFG->enrol_remotecoursefield and $CFG->enrol_remoteuserfield). So I replaced the line... $extcourse = $extcourse_obj->{$CFG->enrol_remotecoursefield}; with... if (empty($extcourse_obj->{$CFG->enrol_remotecoursefield})) {// Oracle might return field name in UPPERCASE! $extcourse = $extcourse_obj->{strtoupper($CFG->enrol_remotecoursefield)}; } else { $extcourse = $extcourse_obj->{$CFG->enrol_remotecoursefield}; } AND I replaced the line... array_push($extenrolments, $crs_obj->{$CFG->enrol_remoteuserfield}); with... if (empty($crs_obj->{$CFG->enrol_remoteuserfield})) { // Oracle might return field name in UPPERCASE! array_push($extenrolments, $crs_obj->{strtoupper($CFG->enrol_remoteuserfield)}); } else { array_push($extenrolments, $crs_obj->{$CFG->enrol_remoteuserfield}); } AND for completeness I include the change made in the above comment, replace the line... $courselist[] = $fields_obj->enrolremotecoursefield; with... if (empty($fields_obj->enrolremotecoursefield)) { // Oracle might return field name in UPPERCASE! $courselist[] = $fields_obj->ENROLREMOTECOURSEFIELD; } else { $courselist[] = $fields_obj->enrolremotecoursefield; } The 3 changes are included in the attached enrol.php (from the 20080813 Moodle 1.9.2 Weekly build). This fix is safe because it is only triggered if the expected object property does not exist and then it assumes that the reason for the code failure is that Oracle or some other culprit has returned the record with the column names in upper case. NOTE: For this fix the administrator does NOT need to change the (Courses->Enrolments->External Database) remote database fields to UPPERCASE (e.g. "enrol_remotecoursefield" and "enrol_remoteuserfield"). This will avoid people hitting the bug and then having to try workarounds. I believe the reason that this bug did not appear in Moodle 1.8 was because of the setuplib.php changes for ADODB_ASSOC_CASE. I probably should have used isset() but I have tested with empty(). Alan.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2checkout.com TOS
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, The accreditation from the awarding body for my elearning site customisations was for IOSH - Institude of Occupational Safety & Health. I believe OSHA is the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, which is pretty much the American equivalent to the HSE - Health and Safety Executive and IOSH combined from my understanding. I am unsure of OSHA's particular requirements to satisfy compliancy for elearning courses. You really need to ask them directly, however I would suspect that OSHA would prefer a SCORM elearning format, but don't quote me on that (we don't use SCORM btw ). The main issues for my part was ensuring that on-line examinations were in their words 'un-cheatable' which I satisfied by creating an on-line exam module based on the lesson module. Some changes were made for to prevent users accessing any other site contents whilst the examination was underway. That IS of course only applied to each users individual elearning account and IMO is not an effective way of prevent cheating as no-one is necessarily around to invidulate examination attempts. Unless of course the exams were taking in a controlled environment. Again my opinion was quashed as it is left for the tutors which marks the exam attempts to filter those students which have 'word for word' perfect answers. Due to the marking criteria the modle answers are worded in such a way that is unnatural for a human to phrase, so it becomes very obiovus when a user is somehow 'cheating' based on these modle answers. The modle answers are particularly concise, almost bullet points even for essay (long answer) type questions/answers. They were also particularly interested in interactivity for questions / quizzes within the content. I had (again) created another module based upon lesson mod and integrated new questions types that are found within the HotPot module, which allowed for drag & drop, jumbled sentence and a number of other question types not natively found within the lesson module. So i'd really look in to securing your site while students are under going examinations and making sure you have plenty of interactivity, however you wish to acheive this. We recently had an audit by IOSH and have recoded an upgraded version of our customisations from a 1.6.4 to a 1.8.8 moodle. IOSH were very happy with how we handled everything in terms of administration and we have built up a good relationship with them. They did stipulate that ALL exam attempts should be recorded, even the failed attempts, which we were not doing until our recent audit. Apparently we had a 100% pass rate, the highest out of any accredited provider. The reason for this is due to that fact that with the courses we provide students are allowed to reattempt if they have failed so long as a 10 day grace period is adhered to before a re-attempt. This effectively meant that we simply informed the students they failed and could retake a different exam in 10 days. As we send a monthly report to IOSH containing the results it was only the passing students that were sent as failed attempts were removed from our system; and any failures were not required to be sent. Originally IOSH did not stipulate they required ALL attempts pass or fail until our recent audit. I must say though, the inital accreditation was particularly difficult to satisfy and IOSH were very thorough in testing our elearning site in terms of both technical requirements and course content. They did however provide great feedback as to what exactly they wanted to see in the elearning site and their suggestions for improving content. Once the accreditation was gained everything has pretty much been smooth sailing .... I'm not sure if i can help you further, but you can always ask and I'll see if I can shed any light from my experiences. PS. Sorry for the length of time taken to responde, i've only just spotted your query. All the best and I hope you can satisfy their requirements. We have had an interest in providing OSHA courses ourselves and would be very interested to know what you find. Perhaps a collaboration may be good idea? Steve

"; $header .= "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Paypal Error
ResponsesInList.Text: This seems to be a recurring issue with few answers - as I've just had the same problem and fixed it I thought I'd post up my fix. Hope it helps others having a hard time getting this set up. In my case the issue was not with Moddle at all but with the way you must set up your PayPal account which is not well documented either here on on the PayPal site itself. The problem is that PayPal must know how to submit the information back to the moodle installation to confirm that payment has been made and received. The process is: (1) User clicks on pay (2) Moodle sends details to PayPal account (3) PayPal handles the transaction (4) PayPal returns details and a code to Moodle (This is where it breaks!) (5) Moodle confirms details (inc. the code) with PayPal (anti-spoof...) (6) PalPay return confirmation to Moodle (7) Moodle enrols student So, the problem is how to let PayPal know where to send the payment details. The moodle script handling the payments is: http:// path/to/moodle/ enrol/paypal/ipn.php You must have a premier or business PayPal account - the ordinary account does not have the facility to process instant payments. Upgrading is free so why not do it? Then (1) click on edit profile (2) Go to "instant payment notification preferences" under "Selling Preferences" (if this isn't there you need to upgrade your account) (3) click edit (4) Check the box and put the ipn.php URL into the box (5) save Now, with any luck, your payments will go through correctly. If you upgraded to Premiere then you can only accept payments from other PayPal accounts - going up to a full business account should allow you to accept payments from anyone with a email address via credit card (but I've not done this myself). Hope this helps anyone having the same problem.

ResponsesInList.Text: The PayPal setting for the IPN was not the answer. But I did figure out my problem. My site got hacked earlier in the month. As a result, my site was being flooded with requests from Wordpress sites for the spam pages. In my zeal to block bad traffic, I did a mod-rewrite in my .htaccess file to deny all Wordpress user agents and all blank user agents. It was this last part that was the problem. I was blocking the IPN request from PayPal as it comes in with a blank User-Agent. To see if this is what is happening to you, you can try to use PayPal's IPN tester (it will tell you that your IPN request is forbidden) or you can look at your access_log. Dig into it and see if the requests for your IPN url (/enrol/paypal/ipn.php) results in 403 or 200 when it comes from PayPal. You can tell its PayPal because of the blank or "-" user agent. That'll teach me to tighten my security

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please Help--New Person
ResponsesInList.Text:
The data must be exported to a .csv (Comma Separated Value) text format see below. Upload users Firstly, note that it is usually not necessary to import users in bulk - to keep your own maintenance work down you should first explore forms of authentication that do not require manual maintenance, such as connecting to existing external databases or letting the users create their own accounts. See the Authentication section in the admin menus. If you are sure you want to import multiple user accounts from a text file, then you need to format your text file as follows: Each line of the file contains one record Each record is a series of data separated by commas The first record of the file is special, and contains a list of fieldnames. This defines the format of the rest of the file. Required fieldnames: these fields must be included in the first record, and defined for each user `username, password, firstname, lastname, email` Default fieldnames: these are optional - if they are not included then the values are taken from the primary admin `institution, department, city, country, lang, auth, timezone` Optional fieldnames: all of these are completely optional. The course names are the "shortnames" of the courses - if present then the user will be enrolled as students in those courses. Group names must be associated to the corresponding courses, i.e. group1 to course1, etc. `idnumber, icq, phone1, phone2, address, url, description, mailformat, maildisplay, htmleditor, autosubscribe, course1, course2, course3, course4, course5, group1, group2, group3, group4, group5, type1, type2, type3, type4, type5, role1, role2, role3, role4, role5, emailstop` Commas within the data should be encoded as &#44 - the script will automatically decode these back to commas. For Boolean fields, use 0 for false and 1 for true. Types are used to tell Moodle whether the user is a student or a teacher if a corresponding course exists (e.g. type2 corresponds to course2). 1 = Student, 2 = Editing Teacher, and 3 = Non-editing Teacher. If type is left blank, or if no course is specified, the user is default to student. For courses use the short name; for groups use group name; for roles use id. Note: If a user is already registered in the Moodle user database , this script will return the userid number (database index) for that user, and will enrol the user as a student in any of the specified courses WITHOUT updating the other specified data. Here is an example of a valid import file: 
```text
username, password, firstname, lastname, email, lang, idnumber, maildisplay, course1, group1, type1


 jonest, verysecret, Tom, Jones, jonest@someplace.edu, en, 3663737, 1, Intro101, Section 1, 1


 reznort, somesecret, Trent, Reznor, reznort@someplace.edu, en_us, 6736733, 0, Advanced202, Section 3, 3
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Ext DB Enrollment - Course End Date crosses Calendar Year
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I am using Ext DB Enrollment with great success within Moodle. But, I've recently run into a problem where the course end date crosses a calendar year - for example I have course with a start date of 11/28/2009 and an end date of 1/9/2010. When those dates are brought over into Moodle, the integration chokes. It appears to be ignoring the year and when it calculates the course weeks it gets a negative number. The logic I am using in the enrol.php to calculate the course end date is below. I think it is right. I am wondering if anyone can see any problems with it or suggest other areas within Moodle that might be called by this file that might cause the date calculation to not include the year properly. if(!empty($CFG->enrol_enddate)){ // Convert dates to UNIX time $arr_startdate = date_parse($course->startdate); $starttime = mktime(0,0,0,$arr_startdate['month'],$arr_startdate['day'],$arr_startdate['year']); $arr_enddate = date_parse($course->enddate); $endtime = mktime(0,0,0,$arr_enddate['month'],$arr_enddate['day'],$arr_enddate['year']); //Set number of Weeks in a course

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ext DB Enrollment - Course End Date crosses Calendar Year
ResponsesInList.Text:
This part of the code is wrong 
```text
$course->numsections = date('W',$endtime)-date('W',$starttime)+1;
```
 You get the week number of the year for both dates and then substract it. Week number of the year doesn't include the year (obviously ), that's why you get a negative quantity: 11/28 has always a greater week number than 1/9. You could substract both Unix dates (which gives you the date difference in seconds, always a positive quantity for end dates later than start dates) and then convert it back to weeks by dividing it by 604800 (60 60 24*7 seconds in a week) and rounding it to the next integer. Something like: 
```text
$course->numsections = (int)(ceil(($endtime - $starttime) / 604800))
```
 Saludos,
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ext DB Enrollment - Course End Date crosses Calendar Year
ResponsesInList.Text: Even though I've been guilty of using it in the past, epoch time is actually not the best way to do things, due to, among other things, year 2038 issues. If you can afford a call to the db backend, have the db do the calculation, or use a library that will let you determine the interval between two dates.

ResponsesInList.Title: ldap_sync_users problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi - I have LDAP working on out server to authenticate users, but am trying to move to the next stage of using auth_ldap_sync_users.php to Sync moodle records to our AD. However when I run auth_ldap_sync_users.php I get the following SQL message(s): Configuring temp table connecting to ldap + 1000 users Illegal mix of collations (utf8_unicode_ci,IMPLICIT) and (utf8_general_ci,IMPLICIT) for operation '=' SELECT u.id, u.username FROM mdl16_user u LEFT JOIN mdl16_extuser e ON u.idnumber = e.idnumber WHERE u.auth='ldap' AND u.deleted='0' AND e.idnumber IS NULL Illegal mix of collations (utf8_general_ci,IMPLICIT) and (utf8_unicode_ci,IMPLICIT) for operation '=' SELECT e.idnumber,1 FROM mdl16_extuser e LEFT JOIN mdl16_user u ON e.idnumber = u.idnumber WHERE u.id IS NULL OR (u.id IS NOT NULL AND u.deleted=1) I've had a look at the Database and cannot find the table mdl16_extuser, could this be the problem? Ive checked all my tables and they are all utf8_unicode. If I run the page again with debugging on I get: Parse error : parse error, unexpected T_STRING in C:\VLE\auth\ldap\auth_ldap_sync_users.php on line 22 I am running moodle 1.6.3+, on server 2003 & IIS My tech guys seem to be of little help and it would ease admin if i could get this working - Thanks in advance. Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ldap_sync_users problem
ResponsesInList.Text:
The mdl16_extuser is a temporary table that's created on the fly by auth_ldap_sync_users.php and removed as soon as the script finishes. So it's not surprising you can't find it It seems MySQL is creating the temporary table with a different UTF-8 enconding (utf8_general_ci) than your normal tables encoding (utf8_unicode_ci). I just don't know why, but you can try forcing the encoding in the code. Edit C:\VLE\auth\ldap\lib.php and around line 1513 (line number for 1.6.4+) you'll see code that reads: 
```text
execute_sql('CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ' . $CFG->prefix .'extuser (idnumber VARCHAR(64), PRIMARY KEY (idnumber)) TYPE=MyISAM',false);
```
 and change it to read: 
```text
execute_sql('CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ' . $CFG->prefix .'extuser (idnumber VARCHAR(64), PRIMARY KEY (idnumber)) TYPE=MyISAM CHARACTER SET utf8 COLLATE utf8_unicode_ci',false);
```
 and see if it helps. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ldap_sync_users problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Iñaki, Thanks for you help. Changing the code above has fixed the script so that it runs! - I had a feeling I had to make a change in the SQL but was not confident in what or where to put it. Thanks again Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ldap_sync_users problem
ResponsesInList.Text: We had the same problem in Moodle 1.8.3 I changed line 360 to reflect the above in auth/ldap/auth.php and it fixed the problem. Inaki, should I put a bug report in? Please advise? I have also heard that this might be a mysql bug ( http://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=27534 ) Interested to know your thoughts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ldap_sync_users problem
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd say this is more of a MySQL configuration issue than a Moodle bug (and I'm not sure this is the same problem than the MySQL bug you reference to). You need to make sure you configure your MySQL client settings and your MySQL server settings to use the same collation (in addition to use the UTF-8 character set). Moodle can't know what collation type you specified for your tables/colums, so it just specifies the UTF-8 character which in turn makes MySQL to use the default collation (utf8_general_ci). If your tables/colums are using an incompatible collation, then you need to either patch Moodle to specify your particular collation (like I suggested above) or convert your tables/colums to the default collation (this can be easily be done with phpmyadmin, for example). Anyway is up to you to open a bug if you feel this should be addressed in a different way Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: "This course is not enrollable at the moment"
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Aharon, Not sure if you found an answer yet, but my school experienced something similar after we installed an enrollment plug in. A couple of questions first: What version of Moodle are you running? Is this a consistent error across all courses? And lastly, do you have a backup copy of the Moodle database that you could refer back to for comparison's sake? In our case, we had installed a plug in that updates student enrollment in courses from the Banner/Luminus student information system. Many users received this error and had duplicate profiles after the integration with Banner. Based upon conversations with the plugin's developer and with some of our support staff, we saw that the Moodle Networking setting was different for these users. (This is mnethostid in the user table in the db). Changing this setting corrected the error for the users and allowed them to enter their courses. Of course the enrollment method we are using is different, so I'm not certain that this will work for you. However, you may want to study the users table closely and compare it to an older copy of the database, if possible. Hope this helps, Nick

To ensure we have a fallback in case things go horribly wrong in September I duplicated our current enrolment plugin folder, changed every instance of the enrolment plugin name to 'pluginname09' (folder, code, everything!) to indicate the year we changed the plugin, but it continues to use the old plugin's config settings. After a bit of investigation I find that in admin/enrol_config.php the enrolment plugin's name should only be 'English letters': 10: $enrol = required_param('enrol', PARAM_ALPHA); ...so it is using the old plugin's settings (but quietly). Is there any major reason for this? Adding '09' to the end of my edited plugin's name is certainly easier than renaming the whole thing (especially as the changes are minor) but looks like I'll have to or bad things will happen! P.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrolment plugin name can't have numbers in it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually no plugins can have digits in their names. I've been tripped up by this myself (qti2 in my case). I have no idea if this was a conscious decision or just a 'feature'.

I may follow Ubuntu's lead: the next one can be called 'barney'. Suggestions happily taken for the remainder of the alphabet! ;) P.

ResponsesInList.Title: Simplifying enrolment with multiple courseID's per course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all. Forgetting Moodle for a second, and I guess this must apply to more colleges than just us: we have courses which have up to four course codes relating to them. The college needs these different course codes (I believe it comes from having different funding streams although there may be other reasons) but the end result is still just one course, no matter which code you enrolled onto. We've previously got around this by having one (meta/parent) course set up with all the course resources, materials, assessments and so on in it, and then having one child course per course code required. It's messy (four courses instead of one) but it does work. We want to change this. We currently use RestianXML to enrol students onto their courses (linking the course code in our college systems with the 'short name' field in Moodle), but what we want to do now is attribute more than one course code to each course. So: I am in the process of rewriting the Restian enrolment plugin to allow multiple course codes for each course, but I wondered has any of this already been done? (This is an issue I also had to deal with when using Blackboard). I can see nothing similar in the Mods and Plugins database and again nothing in this forum which suggests this has been attempted before. Solution 1: I was thinking of a new database table holding all the course codes for a given course, but it might be overkill, and too much tinkering with core code. Solution 2: Add comma separated values to the courseid field (I'll work on populating that field another day) e.g. 'cc100,cc110,cc120', manually query the mdl_courses table for the courseid field, explode it into an array and check each item in turn.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Simplifying enrolment with multiple courseID's per course
ResponsesInList.Text: I think we're doing what you're talking about. In our situation we have a course listed in 2 programs with different unique identifiers (idnumber field in moodle) but both are the same course. We maintain a simple translation table that our enrollment is passed through before moodle gets it. We use database enrollment and some IMS Enrollment too. The translation table is maintained by a simple web interface where you can add or delete rows. For example course01 and course02 are the same. We do a translation of course02 -> course01. In moodle course01 has the enrollments for both courses. -- S

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External database enrolment synchronization
ResponsesInList.Text: The problem is not the tables. The problem is the enrolments of a user are stored inside the user session as part of the login process (to cache them there and avoid lots of expensive database queries at each page load). So even if you modify the role_assignment table (which is what enrol_database_sync.php does), the user session cache is not updated. Which means the user doesn't see the changes. The only way to 'update' the session cache is by logging out and logging in again. Saludos. Iñaki.

```text
MDL-4207
 Don't overwrite modified user profile values with
    // empty 
LDAP
 values when 'unlocked if empty' is set. The purpose
    ...
```

```text
MDL-4207
 Don't overwrite modified user profile values with

    ...
```
 should do it. I'm not absolutely sure of the full implications of removing that stripslashes() call, as far as I've seen, it shouldn't be security hole. Saludos.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP AD enrollment problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks a lot for the information I think I might have found the bug. I'd bet you have the ID Number field mapped to distinguishedName as 'on create', instead of 'on login'. There is an inconsistent way in the way create_user_record() and update_user_record() handle the information they get from the authentication plugin, via ger_userinfo(). The former takes the values as is, and then calls addslashes() to store them in the database, while the latter does a stripslashes() on the values first, then calls addslashes() to store them in the database. All of this doesn't matter at all, as long as there are no 'special' LDAP characters in the values. As soon as we have one of those values, they get quoted in the way the RFCs state, which basically means some '\' are added here and there. And this is where the fun starts with all that addslashes/striplashes game. If I'm right, modifying create_user_record() to behave in the same way update_user_record() does (plus the patch I published before), should fix the issue. The attached patch does exactly that. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Paypal Sandbox
ResponsesInList.Text: Your questions... (1): Outside the sandbox you do not need HTTPS, inside I can't remember. (2): The non-sandbox stuff does seem to be stable. (3): Does work with hosting service although you will have seen from one of my Posts that I needed to put in a bug fix when the hosting provider was using Squid proxy. I have debug code for ipn.php which monitors the IPN request back from Paypal and sends e-mails back from the server to an e-mail address to let one monitor any errors. Nearly all errors in IPN will result in the error message that you get. I have attached the debug version of ipn.php if you are interested in looking at debug output. You will need to change all the " yourmail@yourdomain.com " to your own e-mail. This debug code matches the latest ipn.php in CVS . I would be willing to help interpret debug output. Alan.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Paypal Sandbox
ResponsesInList.Text: What seems to be happening here is that the IPN callback from Paypal (ipn.php) is happening after the return to the user (return.php). So when return.php gets control it sees the payment has not (yet) been received. There are a number of options here... - Use the the real Paypal and see does the problem disappear. Other people are using the plugin live successfully. - Change the wording of lang/en_utf8/moodle.php line:1169 $string['paymentsorry'] to reflect the fact that the payment is likely to have succeeded (rather than failed) and the user should continue to the course. - Code could be added to return.php to keep refreshing the page until payment is complete. Alan.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ext DB Enrollment - Create Course only when instructor logs in?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Janet, I had the same problem and my solution was: As Iñaki says, I built a DB view (courses_for_moodle)on ext. DB with the courses we want Moodle create. And then point the external db enrolment plugin to the view. In addiction, we add a new column in the courses table (ext. DB) named "visible_for_moodle" (default is false). The "courses_for_moodle" view only see courses from course table (ext. DB) if "visible_for_moodle" is true. I made a very simple program where teachers says "I want create a Moodle course from this course (course from ext. DB). This program put "visible_for_moodle" to true for this course (on ext. DB). Then, the enrol plugin can already view this external course (because teacher says he will use it on the simple program) on "courses_for_moodle" view. Of course you can modify the enrol code (it's not dificult) but as much as you modify it, more dificults with new versions of Moodle you'll have. Good luck,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teacher Enrolment
ResponsesInList.Text: There is a catch-22 situation, in that you can only be a teacher inside a course. And so before the course is created, you cannot be a teacher in it. That is why there is a separate role "Course creator". You need to go into Admin -> Users -> Permissions -> Assign system roles, and give those people you want to be able to create courses the 'Course creator' role. When these people create a new course, they will automatically be made a teacher in the new course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help with Categories and Courses
ResponsesInList.Text:
I think a solution is to make one Main Category and then make four courses with Meta course option NO Example: Four courses in the main category each course with a key Course Beginner Course Intermediate Course Advanced Course Business Make for each course an invisible subcategory . (Change this option ( allowvisiblecoursesinhiddencategories ) to YES )
Place all of the courses of each section to its subcategory Change the option (Meta course) to YES when adding the courses to each category with the key and choose its child. Example (Course Beginner) When a user logs in they will see four courses (it doesn't matter that they are not categories!) they still see the list (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced and Business) when they click on a course and put their enrollment key they will automatically get access to all the courses in the subcategory of that course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unenrollment in enrol plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: I am not sure exactly what you need, but the following code does an unenrol and could be called from a plugin... function unenrolstudent($userid, $modulename) { // Student may (or may not be) enrolled in this module // This is from a POST so has slashes (if it comes from elsewhere you must use addslashes() on $modulename) if (!empty($userid)) { $coursetoremove = get_record('course', 'fullname', $modulename); if (!empty($coursetoremove)) { if ($role = get_default_course_role($coursetoremove)) { $ context = get_context_instance(CONTEXT_COURSE, $coursetoremove->id); if (role_unassign($role->id, $userid, 0, $context->id)) { // Will come in here even if did not have role... mark_context_dirty($context->path); $message = ''; $user = get_record('user', 'id', $userid); if (!empty($user->firstname))  $message .= $user->firstname; if (!empty($user->lastname)) $message .= ' ' . $user->lastname; if (!empty($role->name)) $message .= ' as ' . $role->name; $message .= ' in ' . stripslashes($modulename); // ' upload ' needed to stop URL from being mangled add_to_log($coursetoremove->id, 'upload', 'roles unassign', '/admin/roles/assign.php?contextid=' . $context->id . '&roleid=' . $role->id, $message); } } } } } You do not need the add_to_log() bit. Alan.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrollment Patch with SubCategories
ResponsesInList.Text: As far as I know, nobody has attempted this. The way I'd do it is by having a setting specifying the category separator (e.g. '|'), so we can use a character that is not going to be used in our category names (which can vary form site to site). And then when fetching the category of the course from the external database, analyze the path of the category and created all the (parent) categories needed. For example, if the category is 'Comp. Sc.|1st Year|Comp. Architecture', we'd need to make sure there is a top level 'Comp. Sc.' category (or otherwise create it at that level), then a '1st Year' below the previous one, etc. We'd need to match categories by name (as we don't have the internal IDs available in the external database, as you say), so we'd need to make sure we have no duplicated category names at the same level (which Moodle currently permits). If they are at different levels, we can sort it out. It's just a little more work, but should be doable in a day or so. Saludos. Iñaki.

There are a couple of new settings: Category autocreation (Yes/No) Category separator: the character we use as the category separator in the external database field that holds the category for the course. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cron runs but unconfirmed users not deleted
ResponsesInList.Text: I figured out what the problem was... The bottom half of cron.php is what are called clean up tasks. There is a random number generator (from 0 to 100) and if the number is under 20, then these particular tasks will run. If it 20 or above they will not... so it's hit and miss as to when this section of the cron will actually run. It so happened that everytime I tested it, that section did not run. I forced it to run those tasks as well, and it worked okay. In order to make it run those tasks 100% of the time, change this line in admin/cron.php $random100 = rand(0,100); To this: $random100 = 0; ---------------------------- And just as a side note: picking a random number to determine whether parts of the cron job should run or not seems rather odd to me. Would it not make more sense to timestamp when the last time these clean up tasks ran, and then let them run again every xyz number of hours/days since the last time? Then at least you would know that they are getting run regularly. These tasks include removing unconfirmed users and unenrolling longtimenosee students.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mass Enrollment
ResponsesInList.Text:
Well, for what it's worth, here's our My SQL query. 
```text
INSERT INTO {$CFG->prefix}role_assignments (roleid,contextid,userid,timemodified,modifierid,enrol)
(
SELECT
 r.id AS roleid
 , 
context
.id AS contextid
 , u.id AS userid
 , UNIX_TIMESTAMP() AS timemodified
 , {$impersonate_id} AS modifierid
 , 'manual' AS enrol
FROM
 (
 {$CFG->prefix}context context
 , {$CFG->prefix}course c
 , {$CFG->prefix}role r
 , {$CFG->prefix}user u
 , {$CFG->prefix}user_info_data uid
 , {$CFG->prefix}user_info_field uif
 )
WHERE
 r.shortname = '$role_shortname'
 AND context.contextlevel = 50
 AND uif.shortname = '{$field_shortname}'
 AND uif.id = uid.fieldid
 AND uid.data = c.shortname
 AND c.id = context.instanceid
 AND u.id = uid.userid
 AND u.deleted != 1
 AND u.id NOT IN (SELECT userid FROM {$CFG->prefix}role_assignments WHERE contextid = context.id)
);
```
 $CFG->prefix come from the config.php file. $impersonate_id - we use the admin id. $role_shortname - shortname of role we assign. $field_shortname - we use a "custom field" in a users profile. Probably not relevant to your situation. Hopefully that query will at least help you get a start.

ResponsesInList.Text: I think I need to describe what I'm trying to do a little better. We have a separate student information system that handles student enrolment, billing, etc. I extract Moodle enrolments from this system and use External DB Authentication. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrolment Duration and External DB Enrolment
ResponsesInList.Text: Hmmmm, I'm not sure external DB enrolment is what you really need. The rationale for the external DB enrolment plugin is that the external DB is authoritative with respect to the enrolments. If a given user appears in the external DB, then she is enroled in the course. If she doesn't, then she's unenroled. There's no concept of enrolment duration: either she is or she isn't. So in order to achive what you want, you'd need to remove the students from your externa DB after the right period of time. On the other hand, if you want Moodle to keep track of enrolment durations, then you need to use 'manual' enrolments. That doesn't mean you need to enrol students by hand. You can use 'flat file enrolment' and specify the starting and ending time for the enrolments (beware, you need to use Unix timestamp values here). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: limiting course access
ResponsesInList.Text: We offer online real estate education courses. We have been successful in using Moodle for an online real estate broker pre-examination course and now would like to add several other courses to our site using Moodle. However, we have yet to figure out how to restrict student access to only the course for which a student is enrolled. It seems, based on the way we are now set up, if a student enrolls in and pays for one course, they have access to all courses. Can anyone tell me what setting(s) we need to change to restrict course access to only the one(s) for which the student has paid and enrolled? Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: limiting course access
ResponsesInList.Text: It's because you have enrolled your students in the sitewide role via front page site admin. If you go to site Admin>Users>Permissions>Assign System Roles you'll probably find they are there - take them out of there and only allow them into the course where you want them via the course admin block assign roles option. Also check the default user of your Moodle is not student.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: limiting course access
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you! This was definitely helpful. It does not completely solve the problem if we want students to be able to enroll themselves, but it will work if we enroll them manually. So, for now it solves the problem and we appreciate your help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: limiting course access
ResponsesInList.Text: The way we do it is we have a separate payment system from Moodle. Students sign up and pay through Paypal, but receive no login info immediately. We contact each student directly, and email them the course URL and the enrolment key for the course they paid for. That way our main moodle home page is open to the public but each course is protected with the enrolment key they cannot know unless we know they've paid.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: limiting course access
ResponsesInList.Text: You can always use the moodle paypal plugin. You may allow guests to see your front page. That way you do not have to do any emailing, or bother with enrolment keys. That is how I do it, because I don't want to do any work...that is what software is for...doing the jobs people don't want to do so that they can goof around.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to setup External DB enrolment to default in v1.6.3.?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Antonio, there seems to be a bit of missunderstanding about the default enrolment methods. If you read it carefully, it talks about default interactive methods (emphasis mine). External DB is not an interactive method, so you cannot set it as the default. Interactive methods are used when a user wants to enrol in a given course and that course is enrollable. Then the users needs to do some action (interactively) to enrol in the course. Be it clicking on the 'Yes' button or paying via Paypal or whatever. So if you don't want your users to enrol manually in your courses, you need to: a) enrol them via a non-interactive method (like external db b) set all of your courses as non-enrollable. Go to the settings of each course and choose 'No' in the 'Course enrollable' setting. If you have lots of courses and are 100% sure you want all of them non-enrollable interactively (manual or otherwise), you can execute the following SQL query in your Moodle database (this is valid for 1.6.x, I'm not sure about 1.7.x; you've been warned) 
```text
UPDATE mdl_course SET enrollable = '0';
```
 Don't forget that new courses will have a default value of 'Yes' for this setting. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrollment Summary Report
ResponsesInList.Text: This is just a basic query that could be used to do this select u.firstname as "firstname", u.lastname as "lastname", c.fullname as "course name", p.transtime as "Transaction Time", p.payment_status as "Transaction Status" from mdl_enrol_paypal p JOIN mdl_user u ON p.userid = u.id JOIN mdl_course c ON p.courseid = c.id;

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrollment Summary Report
ResponsesInList.Text: SELECT u.firstname as "firstname", u.lastname as "lastname", c.fullname as "course name", p.transtime as "Transaction Time", p.payment_status as "Transaction Status" from mdl_enrol_paypal p JOIN mdl_user u ON p.userid = u.id JOIN mdl_course c ON p.courseid = c.id GROUP BY c.id, p.transtime ORDER BY c.id, p.transtime ASC; That will spit it out grouped by the Course name and With Ascending dates, sorry for the lack of organization on that previous post.

ResponsesInList.Title: Is external database UNenrollment too dangerous
ResponsesInList.Text: We had a big problem last week when the feed to our enrolment database broke halfway through an update. Result - lots of students getting unenrolled from their courses. Not the end of the world as they got back in when the problem was fixed, but what was a problem was that they all got removed from their groups. It strikes me that unenrolment is a bit dangerous, particularly in that it takes the complete lack of data as an instruction to do quite a drastic operation. I'm struggling to think how it can be improved and made more robust. Any suggestions? My first couple of ideas (neither of which would have helped us) are: * Do a check on the recordcount of the database. If it is empty do nothing. Nobody gets unenrolled (scenario, tables are valid but feed is broken, no data) * Add an option for switching off unenrolling. There is no provision for this at the moment. Anything else? Any better ideas?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is external database UNenrollment too dangerous
ResponsesInList.Text: I think the first idea is a bit problematic. If you really want every single user unenrolled, there's no way to do it :-O The second one is more appealing, as long as you set it to unenrol users by default (don't break user expectations ). But it adds Yet Another Configuration Option(tm). Maybe we could design the ext. db. settings page with a 'Standar settings' and a 'Advanced settings' look (much like user's profiles) so we don't end with very large settings pages. Anyway, I think The Right Way(tm) to handle this would be by using transactions on the enrolment database updates. Either the transaction finishes with a commit and you have everything in place, or it rollbacks to the previous state and nothing is lost. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is external database UNenrollment too dangerous
ResponsesInList.Text: Zero record idea... I take your point, but would anybody *really* want to completely empty their database to remove *all* their enrollments? I can't think of a scenario for that. Don't unenrol option.. I genuinely think that this an omission. You really may not want students to be unenrolled (for example, we have some moodle courses that persist well beyond the date on which the course "officially" finishes), and there is no way to do this. However, transactions, a very good point. That also means I can blame somebody else for the problems

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is external database UNenrollment too dangerous
ResponsesInList.Text: You really may not want students to be unenrolled (for example, we have some moodle courses that persist well beyond the date on which the course "officially" finishes), and there is no way to do this. Yes, this is a plausible scenario. But then you have another problem here: you want some enrolments to persist (those of the 'persistent' courses), but I'm pretty sure you don't want all of your enrolments to do the same. But this setting is global. It's all or nothing, so you don't really have a suitable solution. The only way I see to achive this is by 'tagging' the relevant courses as having persistent enrolments, no matter what the source of those enrolments is (manual, db, ldap, etc.). And then attaching/detaching that persistancy to the enrolments themselves when you tag/untag the course, to make the code easier and more scalable. But this is really opening a new can of worms Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: DB Enrolment Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Anybody I'm new to moodle & have been setting up a new installation for my college using moodle 1.9.2. The DB enrolment plugin the comes by default with dosen't support categories in the enrolment DB for courses, so I downloaded Iñaki Arenaza's enrolment plugin from: http://orodruin.escomposlinux.org/~iarenaza/moodle/enrol_db/enrol_db_files_for_19/ Things seemed to be working great until on of my lecturers told me they were not getting all their courses. I checked on here for similar experiences, but didn't see any so I had a look myself & think I have found the problem. In my event log, the following messages were constantly being displayed: User enrolled to course 08/09|33429|NSE1A, but there is more than one course with that value in the enrolment database (in field courseid) In enrol.php in the get_course_details function, there is an SQL statement that reads: $query = "SELECT $columns FROM {$CFG->enrol_coursetable} " . "WHERE {$CFG->enrol_courseid} = '$courseid'"; I think, because my enroloment table has multiple entries against it (a tutor & multiple students), more than 1 row is being returned & the enclosed IF statement is returning an error... I added a DISTINCT statement to the query & every started working properly. $query = "SELECT DISTINCT $columns FROM {$CFG->enrol_coursetable} " . "WHERE {$CFG->enrol_courseid} = '$courseid'"; I'm not sure if there are any other implications to this, but if you are reading this Iñaki, perhaps you can tell me if I did the right thing? Also, do you know if your code will be added to the main Moodle distribution? I find it a bit strange that this functionality is not already there? PS.. Thanks for all the work you do... This enrolment plugin is great..

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: DB Enrolment Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Andrew, I almost missed your post! (a bit busy with the start of the semester and all that ) The plugin assumes you have two different tables: One with the enrolment data, where you have your tutor/students/whatever-roles-you-use related to their courses A different table with just the course data (shortname, fullname, category, etc.) This second table is assumed to have unique records for each course, and that's why there's no DISTINCT qualifier in the SQL query: there is (supposedly) no need for it. I think I'm going to add the DISTINCT qualifier anyway. It doesn't hurt when you don't have multiples entries for the same course (what the plugin has assumed so far) and it helps a lot when you do Regarding the question about adding the code to the main Moodle distribution, we have tried in the past, although not too much. Given that we have added another interesting feature(*), maybe we'll try again this October, when Martin Dougiamas comes to Spain to the Spanish Moot (*) You can use existing courses as templates for the newly autocreated course. But the feature is that is completely copies the template course to the new course, including sections , activities , blocks, course settings (visibility, etc.). Given that the copy operation is quite heavy, you can decide if you autocreate courses during user login or only during batch processing via enrol_database_sync.php. I inted to publish a patch as soon as the my work load decreases a bit In the meantime, those brave enough can browse the patch at this temporary git repository: http://git.eteo.mondragon.edu/gitweb?p=enrol-db.git;a=summary Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Should one plug-in overwrite another and should manual trump all?
ResponsesInList.Text: Interesting topic... My LMB/Banner module has the same behavior - The thing is, is I can think of instances where you would want the plugin to unenrol a user automatically. Lets say you manually add a user to a course because their paperwork is being slow and classes are starting. Then the enrolment is added in Banner, and comes across to the plugin. Now in the currently 'shipping' version, it will re-enrol them, chaning it to lmb, but in the new version I'm working on, it doesnt do a role_assign if the user is already in that role/ context (to minimize db updates for Postgres ). Now if the student later drops the course, that plugin is still going to want to (and the desired effect is to) drop them. At the very least I would think this should be a param into the role_assign and role_unassign functions, that if you pass true, then it will do it, even if things dont match. Then at least the dev has to make a concious decision to do it - or can make it on option in their settings area to allow it to override. I guess another option could be to allow the user to specify the 'priority' of different methods at a site level.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How does flat file work?
ResponsesInList.Text: Here's the comments from inside the code, which explain how the file should work: * Comma separated file assumed to have four or six fields per line: *   operation, role, idnumber(user), idnumber(course) [, starttime, endtime] * where: *   operation        = add | del *   role             = student | teacher | teacheredit *   idnumber(user)   = idnumber in the user table NB not id *   idnumber(course) = idnumber in the course table NB not id *   starttime        = start time (in seconds since epoch) - optional *   endtime          = end time (in seconds since epoch) - optional The other thing to watch out for is to make sure the file is accessible to apache - I put mine inside the data directory when I eventually realized why it wasn't working.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How does flat file work?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How does flat file work?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'll support the wish for the ability to set Groups during flat-file enrolment. The setup where I would find it especially useful is as follows: If various 'dummy' courses exist with the purpose of holding lists of students (e.g. for year groups) and enabling 'real' courses to be defined as metacourses and take their enrolments from the the dummy courses there is the benefit of single lists to maintain which can then provide multiple courses with correct, up-to-date registration lists. However, some courses might use groups. These can not be set in / picked up from the dummy courses. ((i) Group information is not passed on to metacourses in any case; (ii) Even if it were there might be different group structures in different real courses, so it would not,in general, make sense to maintain a single group structure in the dummy course (although it might be applicable in particular situations). If flat-file enrolment is used the option to update existing users (to set groups) also updates passwords - not a happy situation for active users who might be involved in other Moodle courses to find their password reset. So the problem is that students can be added very neatly to the real courses from the singly maintained lists with just a few clicks, however there is then a substantial manual task in individually identifying / adding students to groups via the web interface. This could be a prohibitively time consuming / laborious task. Some sort of offline, bulk preparation of group enrolments would seem to be a significant 'missing link' that currently forces a heavy manual task on what would otherwise be a convenient enrolment facility for situations where metacourses can be used to good effect. It's almost there... it would just need a way of specifying 'no password change' but allowing other changes (groups) to take effect. A blank password field could be one way to accomplish this (although at present it resets the password instead, which I guess might be a useful facility to retain in some situations). I'm not sure whether I've missed some other setup that would achieve the above? The above is on 1.6. Is there enough interest to request this facility as standard? I'd guess it is a simple one to implement (small UI addition and corresponding test during upload to bypass password change) and would significantly enhance the enrolment facility.

ResponsesInList.Title: Passing Parameter to "table"
ResponsesInList.Text: I just discovered something that might be of interest to others. Maybe it was obvious all along, but I just learned it (not having needed it before). You can pass a parameter to a user defined function in your external database when you specify the table name in the setup screen for external db enrollments. For example, if your database has a user defined function named "mdl_udfEnrollment" that returns a table containing the fields you need for the Moodle enrollment plugin, and you want to pass the name of the particular moodle site, let's say "moodle1", so that the UDF could tailor its lookup of enrolledments accordingly, you could specify the table as mdl_udfEnrollment(\'moodle1\'). (Why do this? Well, imagine that multiple moodle sites all draw enrollments off some common database-- or tell your own story where this might be useful to you...) Anyway, I just wanted to share it with the rest of the Moodle User community.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What is the main use case for the enrolment keyholder?
ResponsesInList.Text: The use case of the enrollment key holder is that in which there would be someone specificly defined who holds the keys and is resposible for sending them out to people who request entrance to classes with keys.  By default the system does what you are expecting, handing the job over to the teacher of the class.  However, perhaps the faculty is not to be responsible for this duty, as in some campuses the petitioning student must take their request for access to the class to an administrative representative who controls the access to courses. In this case I might create a new role for the key holder, and assign them as the keyholder in the internal enrollment settings, so that whenever a student wanted access to a class requiring an enrollment key, they would be directed to the correct person. It is more of a question of mirroring a process than it is about assigning the "right" to hand out keys, as roles who can edit the class settings could edit the enrollment key or send it out if they felt like it. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What is the main use case for the enrolment keyholder?
ResponsesInList.Text: I would start by saying that the default would be that you as the teacher was also the key holder.  But for this example lets say that I am an administrator and my task list includes checking and granting(or denying) enrollment requests.  The Course Creator has made the class and I have the master list of enrollment keys, as it is my specific job to hand them out. 1) A student requests access to an enrollment key locked course which you are teaching in Moodle. 2) The Moodle Site Administrator has set the Enrollment Key Holder to a specific role which I am assigned to.  Moodle offers the student the opportunity to contact me with the request to gain access to your course. 3) The student messages me through the Moodle messaging system that they would like access to the class. 4) I check my messages in Moodle see the request, and grant or deny as appropriate.  (Pre-requisites, capacity, vindictiveness, etc.)  If granted, I send the student the enrollment key they were looking for. 5) The student returns with the enrollment key and enrolls themselves in the class. The issuing of the enrollment keys can be done in any number of different ways.  The Enrollment Key Holder override is there to allow the flexibility to move the job to another position if that is what fits the requirements of an institution.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What is the main use case for the enrolment keyholder?
ResponsesInList.Text: Now we're getting somewhere! We agree on what happens once students enter the picture, but I'm interested in the early stages of the protocol. Specifically, how does the key get into the course settings, and how does the key holder gain his knowledge of the key? You say the administrator has the master list of enrollment keys. Good. Let's say he keeps it on a piece of paper locked in his office safe. The list includes enrollment keys for all current courses as well as courses that haven't been created yet. Consider a new course. Someone must create the course. It could be the administrator, but I'll assume it's a different person, the course creator. I see two cases: The administrator whispers the key to the course creator and the creator enters the key into the course settings. The key holder learns the key from either the administrator or the creator (this does not require any permissions within the course) or by peeking at the course settings (which requires moodle/course:update = Allow). The creator leaves the key field empty. The key holder learns the key from the administrator and enters the key into the course settings (this requires moodle/course:update = Allow). In a highly differentiated work environment, the administrator will typically delegate such mundane matters as the handling of enrollment keys to one or more key holders. These same users may also be responsible for course creation, but to keep it interesting, I'll assume they are different people. Now each key holder has a secret list which he keeps in his office safe. I see two cases: The key holder whispers the key to the course creator and the creator enters the key into the course settings The creator leaves the key empty. The key holder enters the key into the course settings (this requires moodle/course:update = Allow). This seems somewhat more reasonable than the earlier scenario. However it is only completely reasonable if The course creator and the key holder are always the same person The normal teacher is prevented from seeing, much less changing the key

Someone (I will call them a student) who wants online training first has to register with our site, via an email to the person in charge . Once onto the site, all training is free and relatively open to everybody. Trainings are contained in specific courses. We have no instructors only static courses which are open 24/7/365. The student has talked with the training officer at the local agency. The training officer gives the student the enrollment key. As part of the course, the student can print up a certificate. The student turns the certificate into the training officer who places it in the student's file. Ultimately, the agency is responsible for maintaining records of a student's hours of training per year (essentially ceu's). Of course someone may take training from other places besides our agency and that will count with proper documentation. And yes, we print an put a copy of the certificate in our file on the student So the recap. All students are prescreened by our site and qualified to take the internal enrolment courses on our site. The enrollment key is sent to a large group of other people who both supervise and perhaps pay individuals to train. An individual requires pre-approval on the local level to take a course. That is where the enrollment key comes in. I think we change the keys every year. Another example Best Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What is the main use case for the enrolment keyholder?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, To recap: On your site, training officers (who are also keyholders) are responsible for evaluating training requests. They only give keys to people they approve. You say "The student has talked with the training officer at the local agency. The training officer gives the student the enrollment key." So in your case, the Moodle key holder mechanism, (assuming you used it) would only be used to remind forgetful students of who their training officer is, in case they forget the key. It sounds like your site is fairly static in terms of courses, and that procedures are fairly informal. Given that, your approach seems appropriate. In fact, if your case were the MAIN use case, I don't think Moodle would bother providing a special key holder mechanism. So I suspect that the main use case for key holder caters to sites that are highly formal (e.g. 100% online) highly dynamic (courses and teachers in constant flux) and highly differentiated (in terms of who does what). That's the use case I'm looking for.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What is the main use case for the enrolment keyholder?

However, we do not promote, encourage sharing of a course key among students and in fact it technically it might be grounds for a de-certification hearing by the state certifying agency. Yes, our site is fairly static but has a strict student honor code as you can see. The administrators of my site would say it is very formal and informal is completely unacceptable And I agree that I don't really see the use of a keyholder role. ResponsesInList.Title: Multiple "sections"?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everybody- I'm a Moodle newbie but I am very impressed so far. I'm a firefighter with a large urban fire department, with a large MS Access training records database kept at the fire academy. My current job involves a ton of work just to keep this monster working, and I will move us over to Moodle, with a just little help. We (me and the academy's summer intern - a CS grad student, thankfully) have our basic setup running nicely on a windows box, with phpmyadmin, mrbs , and php acceleration added in. The intent is to begin with Moodle as a central record-keeping tool AND a repository for course presentation materials and handouts. Once it does that convincingly, and with less effort than what we have to do now, we'll expand into all the other features. So far, works GREAT. Our difficulty is this: the academy training right now is recorded in MS Access with three key fields: userid, courseid, and completion_date. The course duration varies from 23 weeks down to single day seminars. The thing to keep in mind is the focus on the completion date - the "finish date" which we use to build each FF's master training record and produce college-type transcripts . (We are also a credit-granting agency with a full-time registrar.) In terms of enrolling students, the six month courses and other "longer" courses work fine in Moodle as is. A student would only enroll in such a course once. The single-day training that we have is repetitive, though, and is scheduled in terms of firefighting units , not individual members/students. We know Engine 1 is coming for the drill, as scheduled, but the members working that day will be enrolled/recorded as trained only after they get here. A firefighter may come four times in a year for the same drill - "Tactical Unconscious FF Removal" or "Self-Rescue Rope Refresher." Upon completion of the drill, a hand-written sign-in sheet goes to the data-entry person. Most firefighters and their officers will repeat at least one of the single-day drills during a two-year period. They are essentially re-taking a one-day class. We've looked at groups , restoring courses, etc. and haven't found a solution yet. (One particular drill/class is conducted 300 days a year, and most training is conducted at least once a month.) The solution we desire will let the data-entry person, who is swamped, enroll anyone off of her backlog pile, some of it more than a month old, as well as the current 'today' students. It will let specialty instructors build attendee lists for future multi-week classes that are offerred 4x a year. And, eventually, regular instructors in the classroom will sign in to Moodle and before starting their refresher training Powerpoints or printing their new handouts, they can go around the room and take names/enroll students right from the podium. In short, we need to enroll students in a course, then find and enroll them again in a new "section" of the same course next week or next month, and we need to back-fill 200,000+ training records across 20,000+ active/retired members within 400+ current/archive courses. We've been tempted to add a training_date to the role_ assignment table, then modify the assign.php/html files so when assigning the role 'student' for a course, the user will have to pick a 'section_complete_date.' (the date of training for one-day courses, and the "finish date" for multi-day or multi-week training.) As we say over the radio, "Can anyone advise...?"

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple "sections"?
ResponsesInList.Text: Humm, You have asked a lot of questions. We do training in a sometimes certified environment but as an organization that deals with about 25% of your scope and use Moodle for less than 1/2 of our potential scope from a registrar standpoint. My site administrator talks about the same kinds of things: Goal is to track all training records in a unified system. We are spoiled and have 20 to 60 wireless laptops available for daily "guests", in a addition to laptops for our residential trainees. And we have 3 remote sites connected on a internal network. So if our site had your problem, I would suggested issuing laptops for the day (or just for sign in and then for testing and/or sign out), give the trainees the enrollment key to the course and have them register themselves (maybe even fill out a profile). Have some dedicated workstations just for that purpose. At our sites I would make them take a quiz at the end of the day, and a pass of 80% gets them a copy of a certificate and one emailed mailed to that overworked data entry person and another to the registrar. There are several other options that come to mind. There might be no quiz and the instructor reveals the certificate at 1600 hours so people print up their own. Could have the instructor enter in their score(s) from a piece of paper that would qualify the trainee to open and "print" their certificate. The hard working data entry person prints up a grade sheet, or certificate issue list and double checks it against the signed verified roster. We use certificate but in an older version of Moodle and I think 1.9 certificate has features a registrar might appreciate.

ResponsesInList.Title: Authorize.net enrolment module tip
ResponsesInList.Text: I was getting this error: " This account has not been given the permission (s) required for this request. " I looked into it, and apparently sometime in 2006, as a means of increasing security, Authorize.net prohibited logging in with your password and userid to authenticate your merchant account. Currently, the best (only?) way to authenticate is to use the combination of the "API Login Key" and the "Transaction Key". Fortunately, even though the authorize.net enrolment module's instructions tell you to use your login ID, you can still supply your API Login Key instead and it will work. Just a pointer for those of you getting this cryptic error message. Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Text: Jason: You are on the right track. When a user is assigned the role of student in a course, an entry is made in the table role_assignments . It will typically have a roleid of 5 (legacy student role) and the userid corresponding to the user record in the usertable.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course enrolment information in mdl_role_assignments?
ResponsesInList.Text: Jason: No need to apologize. In fact, chatting with others about it firms my own understanding. In terms of counting students, you should have (at least) one entry in the table role_assignments for each student in your course. It will have that student's userid, a roleid (probably of 5 as a legacy student found in the table role_capabilities), and a contextid corresponding to an entry in the table context . In that table, it will have a contextlevel of 50 and an instanceid that corresponds to the courseid. Items in the context table with contextlevel other than 50 correspond to other elements like course categories, blocks, etc. Their instanceid field will identify those. Because of the great generality, this is not easy to 'get our heads around', but with time it starts making sense. --Gary

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Confirm email modified to enrol directly into course and group.
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not really sure I understand your current workflow. Email authentication is based on the assumption that the user will be able to autoregister him/herself and then choose his/her courses at his/her will. If you already have a process in place for users to apply for particular courses (or even a single course) and you need to enrol that user in the course, email authentication doesn't make much sense to me. Either manual authentication (where the admin creates the account on behalf of the user manuall) or external database authentication (where Moodle pulls the user account details from an external db) makes more sense. Then, once you have the user account created, you can enrol that user into the course, again either manually or by using an external enrolment database. In fact, if you use an external database both for authentication and enrolment and make your courses not open to guests and not enrollable by the users themselves, you can simple send an email to the user with the link to the course page. As the course is not open or enrollable, the user will need to authenticate him/herself, and the external db will provide the enrolment 'credentials' for only the courses the user is enrolled into, and Moodle will forbid the user to enter any other closed/non-enrollable courses. Does this make sense to you? Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: enrolment hierarchy, manual trumping all others

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mass Enrollment without Student ID
ResponsesInList.Text:
I want to assume that it can be found when editing a users profile such as: http://www.mysitename.com/user/editadvanced.php?id=1887&course=15 Where the 1887 could be their studentID? In fact, 1887 is the 'id' of the record for the student in the mdl_user table. What you are looking for is what we call the 'ID number' (that is called 'idnumber' in the mdl_user table), that will be probably empty as you say above. If you have direct access to Moodle's database , you can set the 'idnumber' field directly to anything you want. For example, the username. With something like the SQL sentence below: 
```text
UPDATE mdl_user SET idnumber=username WHERE deleted <> 1;
```
 This way you can use the same value of the username for the enrolments. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Oracle Enrolments not enrolling
ResponsesInList.Text: We had a similar problem in our environment. The first thing that you may want to try is updating to the latest version of MySQL . That may help. You may also want to tweak your enrol.php file like the attached. We had some help from Jonathan ( http://remote-learner.net/ ). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Oracle Enrolments not enrolling
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Todd, Using your enrol file seemed to do the trick. Do you have any further details on what it is doing different - is it just a case issue. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Oracle Enrolments not enrolling
ResponsesInList.Text: Yeah, it appears that this is strictly a field case name issue. The adodb library casts all the Oracle fields to caps but the Moodle code appears to be hard coded to all lower case. We fixed by adding an or clause to the test for matching the values. I believe our developer is in process of getting this reported so it can be updated in core.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Oracle Enrolments not enrolling
